title.zh: 卷八十二 志第五十八 食貨六
title.raw: 卷八十二 志第五十八 食貨六 Volume 82 Treatises 58: Finance and Economics 6

sentences.zh: 上供採造 採造柴炭 採木 珠池 織造 燒造 俸餉 會計

translations.literal: Imperial tribute and procurement; procurement of charcoal and fuel; timber procurement; pearl fisheries; weaving; kiln firing; stipends; accounting.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Tribute and Procurement; Procurement of Charcoal and Fuel; Timber Procurement; Pearl Fisheries; Weaving; Kiln Firing; Stipends; Accounting.

sentences.zh: 採造之事，累朝侈儉不同。

translations.literal: Matters of procurement and tribute differed in extravagance and frugality from reign to reign.
translations.idiomatic: Across successive reigns, imperial procurement and tribute varied widely in extravagance and restraint.

sentences.zh: 大約靡於英宗，繼以憲、武，至世宗、神宗而極。

translations.literal: Roughly, extravagance flourished under Emperor Ying, continued under Xian and Wu, and reached its extreme under Shizong and Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In broad outline, waste set in under the Yingzong emperor, carried on through the Chenghua and Wuzong reigns, and peaked under the Jiajing and Wanli emperors.

sentences.zh: 其事目繁瑣，徵索紛紜。

translations.literal: The categories of business were numerous and minute; levies and requisitions were tangled and confused.
translations.idiomatic: The items multiplied into a maze of petty categories, and demands and requisitions piled up in confusion.

sentences.zh: 最鉅且難者，曰採木。

translations.literal: The greatest and most difficult was called timber procurement.
translations.idiomatic: The largest and hardest burden was timber procurement.

sentences.zh: 歲造最大者，曰織造、曰燒造。

translations.literal: Among annual manufactures, the largest were called weaving and kiln firing.
translations.idiomatic: Of the annual manufacturing programs, weaving and kiln firing were the largest.

sentences.zh: 酒醴膳羞則掌之光祿寺，採辦成就則工部四司、內監司局或專差職之，柴炭則掌之惜薪司。

translations.literal: Wine, fermented liquor, and palace fare were managed by the Court of Imperial Entertainments; when procurement was completed, the four bureaus of the Ministry of Works, the eunuch directorates and offices, or specially dispatched officials took charge; charcoal and fuel were managed by the Directorate for Cherishing Fuel.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments oversaw wine and palace food; once goods were procured, the Ministry of Works bureaus, inner-palace eunuch offices, or ad hoc commissioners handled them; charcoal and firewood fell to the Directorate for Cherishing Fuel.

sentences.zh: 而最為民害者，率由中官。

translations.literal: Yet what harmed the people most generally came from palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the worst harm to the people usually came from eunuch agents of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 明初，上供簡省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, imperial tribute was simple and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, imperial tribute was kept lean and simple.

sentences.zh: 郡縣貢香米、人參、葡萄酒，太祖以為勞民，卻之。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties presented fragrant rice, ginseng, and grape wine; the founding emperor considered this a burden on the people and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: When counties sent fragrant rice, ginseng, and grape wine as tribute, the Hongwu emperor judged it an imposition on the people and declined it.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，光祿卿井泉奏，歲例遣正官往南京採玉面狸，帝叱之曰：「小人不達政體。

translations.literal: Early in the Hongxi reign, the director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Jing Quan, memorialized that each year regular officials were sent to Nanjing to procure masked palm civets; the emperor rebuked him, saying: "Petty men do not understand the substance of government.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongxi reign, Jing Quan, director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, reported the annual dispatch of regular officials to Nanjing for masked palm civets. The emperor snapped at him: "You petty men do not grasp how government should work.

sentences.zh: 朕方下詔，盡罷不急之務以息民，豈以口腹細故，失大信耶！

translations.literal: I have just issued an edict abolishing all non-urgent tasks to give the people rest—how could I, for a trifle of the palate, break great faith!"
translations.idiomatic: I have just proclaimed an end to every nonessential task so the people can recover—would I break that solemn pledge for a mouthful of delicacy?"

sentences.zh: 」宣宗時，罷永樂中河州官買乳牛造上供酥油者，以其牛給屯軍。

translations.literal: " In the Xuande period, he abolished the Yongle practice of Hezhou officials buying dairy cows to make butter for imperial tribute, and gave those cows to garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Under the Xuande emperor, the court ended the Yongle arrangement by which Hezhou officials bought dairy cows for imperial butter and reassigned the animals to garrison farmers.

sentences.zh: 命御史二人察視光祿寺，凡內外官多支及需索者，執奏。

translations.literal: He ordered two censors to inspect the Court of Imperial Entertainments; whenever officials inside or outside over-issued or made improper demands, they were to arrest and report them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent two censors to audit the Court of Imperial Entertainments and ordered them to seize and report any official, inside or outside the court, who over-claimed supplies or extorted goods.

sentences.zh: 英宗初政，三楊當軸，減南畿孳牧黃牛四萬，糖蜜、果品、腒脯、酥油、茶芽、稉糯、粟米、藥材皆減省有差，撤諸處捕魚官。

translations.literal: In the early government of Emperor Ying, with the Three Yangs holding power, they reduced by forty thousand the yellow cattle bred in the southern capital region; sugar, honey, fruit, dried meat, butter, tea shoots, glutinous and non-glutinous rice, millet, and medicinal materials were all cut by varying amounts, and fishing officials throughout the realm were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong emperor first took the throne, the Three Yangs at the helm cut forty thousand head from the southern capital's cattle herds, trimmed sugar, fruit, cured meats, butter, tea, rice, millet, and medicines by varying degrees, and abolished the empire-wide fishing commissioners.

sentences.zh: 即位數月，多所撙節。

translations.literal: Within months of his accession, much was economized.
translations.idiomatic: Within months of his accession, he imposed wide economies.

sentences.zh: 凡上用膳食器皿三十萬七千有奇，南工部造，金龍鳳白瓷諸器，饒州造，鵜硃紅膳盒諸器，營膳所造，以進宮中食物，尚膳監率乾沒之。

translations.literal: In all, more than three hundred and seven thousand dining vessels for imperial use: the southern Ministry of Works made gold dragon-and-phoenix white porcelain and the like; Raozhou made cinnabar-red food boxes and the like; the provisioning kitchens made them to present palace food—and the Directorate of Palace Provisions habitually embezzled them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tableware totaled more than three hundred seven thousand pieces: the southern Ministry of Works supplied gold dragon-and-phoenix white porcelain; Raozhou supplied cinnabar-red food boxes; the provisioning kitchens supplied the rest for palace meals—and the Directorate of Palace Provisions routinely pocketed them.

sentences.zh: 帝令備帖具書，如數還給。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered tallies prepared and written out, and the full count returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered written tallies prepared and every item returned in full.

sentences.zh: 景帝時，從于謙言，罷真定、河間採野味、直沽海口造乾魚內使。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai period, following Yu Qian's advice, he abolished the eunuchs who gathered game in Zhending and Hejian and made dried fish at the Zhigu estuary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign, heeding Yu Qian, the court abolished the eunuchs sent to Zhending and Hejian for game and to the Zhigu estuary for dried fish.

sentences.zh: 天順八年，光祿果品物料凡百二十六萬八千餘斤，增舊額四之一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianshun, fruit and material goods for the Court of Imperial Entertainments totaled more than 1,268,000 jin, an increase of one quarter over the old quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun year 8, fruit and supplies for the Court of Imperial Entertainments reached more than 1.268 million jin—a quarter above the former quota.

sentences.zh: 成化初，詔光祿寺牲口不得過十萬。

translations.literal: Early in Chenghua, an edict fixed livestock for the Court of Imperial Entertainments at no more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign, an edict capped the court's livestock at one hundred thousand head.

sentences.zh: 明年，寺臣李春請增。

translations.literal: The next year, Li Chun of the court requested an increase.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Li Chun of the court asked to raise the quota.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書姚夔言：「正統間，雞鵝羊豕歲費三四萬。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yao Kui said: "During the Zhengtong period, chickens, geese, sheep, and pigs cost thirty to forty thousand a year.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yao Kui said: "Under Zhengtong, poultry and livestock cost thirty to forty thousand a year.

sentences.zh: 天順以來增四倍，暴殄過多。

translations.literal: Since Tianshun it has increased fourfold—waste is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianshun it has quadrupled—far too much is squandered.

sentences.zh: 請從前詔。

translations.literal: Please follow the earlier edict."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the earlier edict be enforced."

sentences.zh: 」後二年，給事中陳鉞言：「光祿市物，概以勢取。

translations.literal: " Two years later, supervising secretary Chen Yue said: "When the Court of Imperial Entertainments buys goods, it generally takes them by force of position.
translations.idiomatic: " Two years later, supervising secretary Chen Yue said: "When the Court of Imperial Entertainments buys supplies, it seizes them by sheer power.

sentences.zh: 負販遇之，如被劫掠。

translations.literal: Peddlers who encountered them felt as if they had been robbed.
translations.idiomatic: Street vendors met them as though at the hands of bandits.

sentences.zh: 夫光祿所供，昔皆足用，今不然者，宣索過額，侵漁妄費也。

translations.literal: What the Court of Imperial Entertainments supplied was once sufficient; that it is not so now is because palace demands exceed quotas and because embezzlement and reckless spending.
translations.idiomatic: The court's provisions once sufficed; they no longer do because palace requisitions exceed the quotas and because officials skim and waste recklessly.

sentences.zh: 」大學士彭時亦言：「光祿寺委用小人買辦，假公營私，民利盡為所奪。

translations.literal: " Grand Secretary Peng Shi also said: "The Court of Imperial Entertainments entrusts petty men with procurement; they use public office for private gain, and the people's profit is wholly seized.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Secretary Peng Shi added: "The court entrusts procurement to petty agents who abuse public office for private gain until nothing is left for the people.

sentences.zh: 請照宣德、正統間例，斟酌供用，禁止買辦。

translations.literal: Please follow the precedents of the Xuande and Zhengtong periods, adjust supplies with discretion, and forbid procurement purchases."
translations.idiomatic: Follow the Xuande and Zhengtong precedents, set supplies at a measured level, and ban procurement buying."

sentences.zh: 」於是減魚果歲額十之一。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the annual quota for fish and fruit was reduced by one tenth.
translations.idiomatic: " The annual fish and fruit quota was then cut by one tenth.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年命光祿減增加供應。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, the Court of Imperial Entertainments was ordered to reduce added supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 1, the court was ordered to roll back the added provisions.

sentences.zh: 初，光祿俱預支官錢市物，行頭吏役因而侵蝕。

translations.literal: At first the Court of Imperial Entertainments all advanced official money to buy goods, and market brokers and clerks thereby embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court advanced official funds for purchases, and brokers and clerks siphoned off the difference.

sentences.zh: 乃令各行先報納而後償價，遂有遊手號為報頭，假以供應為名，抑價倍取，以充私橐。

translations.literal: Then each trade was ordered to deliver goods first and be paid afterward; thereupon idlers styled themselves "report heads," under the name of supplying provisions suppressed prices and took double, filling private purses.
translations.idiomatic: The court then required trades to deliver goods before payment, which spawned loafers calling themselves "report heads" who, in the name of supply, forced down prices and took double their due for private profit.

sentences.zh: 御史李鸞以為言，帝命禁止。

translations.literal: Censor Li Luan reported this; the emperor ordered it forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Luan reported the abuse, and the emperor forbade it.

sentences.zh: 十五年，光祿卿王珩，列上內外官役酒飯及所畜禽獸料食之數，凡百二十事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Wang Heng, listed the amounts of wine, food, and fodder for officials and servants inside and outside the palace and for kept birds and beasts—one hundred and twenty items in all.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15, Wang Heng, director of the court, submitted a list of one hundred twenty items covering wine, meals, and fodder for palace staff and for kept birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 乃降旨，有仍舊者，有減半者，有停止者。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: some items were to remain as before, some halved, some stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: some items unchanged, some halved, some abolished outright.

sentences.zh: 於是放去乾明門虎、南海子貓、西華門鷹犬、御馬監山猴、西安門大鴿等，減省有差，存者減其食料。

translations.literal: Thereupon tigers at Qianming Gate, cats at the Southern Sea Park, hawks and dogs at Xihua Gate, mountain monkeys of the Imperial Stud, large pigeons at Xi'an Gate, and the like were released; reductions varied by item, and for those kept, fodder was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers at Qianming Gate, cats at the Southern Sea Park, hawks and hounds at Xihua Gate, the Imperial Stud's monkeys, and Xi'an Gate's carrier pigeons were released; other items were trimmed by degree, and survivors had their rations cut.

sentences.zh: 自成化時，添坐家長隨八十餘員，傳添湯飯中官百五十餘員。

translations.literal: From the Chenghua period, more than eighty seated household stewards were added, and more than one hundred fifty eunuchs for extra soup and meals.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chenghua reign onward, the court added more than eighty seated household stewards and more than one hundred fifty eunuchs devoted to extra soups and meals.

sentences.zh: 天下常貢不足於用，乃責買於京師鋪戶。

translations.literal: The empire's regular tribute was insufficient for use, so purchases were forced on Beijing shop households.
translations.idiomatic: When routine tribute from across the empire no longer sufficed, the burden was shifted onto Beijing shopkeepers.

sentences.zh: 價直不時給，市井負累。

translations.literal: Prices were not paid in season, and the market towns were burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Payment came late or not at all, and the markets groaned under the debt.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書劉大夏因天變言之，乃裁減中官，歲省銀八十餘萬。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liu Daxia spoke of this because of a heaven-sent anomaly; eunuch staff was then cut, saving more than eight hundred thousand taels of silver a year.
translations.idiomatic: After Minister of War Liu Daxia raised the issue amid celestial warnings, eunuch staff was cut back, saving more than eight hundred thousand taels a year.

sentences.zh: 武宗之世，各宮日進、月進，數倍天順時。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Wu, daily and monthly deliveries from each palace were several times those of the Tianshun period.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wuzong emperor, each palace's daily and monthly deliveries ran several times the Tianshun level.

sentences.zh: 廚役之額，當仁宗時僅六千三百餘名，及憲宗增四之一。

translations.literal: The quota of kitchen servants was only a little more than six thousand three hundred under Emperor Ren; under Emperor Xian it increased by one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen staff numbered barely six thousand three hundred under the Hongxi emperor; the Chenghua emperor raised the quota by a quarter.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，減至四千一百名，歲額銀撙節至十三萬兩。

translations.literal: Early in Shizong's reign it was reduced to four thousand one hundred names, and the annual silver quota was economized to one hundred thirty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign the staff fell to four thousand one hundred and the annual silver outlay was trimmed to one hundred thirty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 中年復增至四十萬。

translations.literal: In his middle years it rose again to four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-reign it had climbed again to four hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 額派不足，借支太倉。

translations.literal: When allotted quotas were insufficient, advances were borrowed from the Grand Canal granary.
translations.idiomatic: When quotas fell short, the court borrowed from the Taicang granary.

sentences.zh: 太倉又不足，乃令原供司府依數增派。

translations.literal: When Taicang too was insufficient, the original supplying prefectures and departments were ordered to increase levies by set amounts.
translations.idiomatic: When Taicang ran dry as well, the original supplying prefectures were ordered to raise their levies proportionally.

sentences.zh: 於是帝疑其乾沒，下禮部問狀，責光祿寺具數以奏。

translations.literal: The emperor then suspected embezzlement, sent the case to the Ministry of Rites for inquiry, and ordered the Court of Imperial Entertainments to submit full accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected embezzlement, referred the matter to the Ministry of Rites, and demanded a full accounting from the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 帝復降旨詰責，乃命御史稽覈月進揭帖，兩月間省銀二萬餘兩，自是歲以為常。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued an edict of rebuke and ordered censors to audit monthly delivery tallies; within two months more than twenty thousand taels of silver were saved, and thereafter this became annual practice.
translations.idiomatic: After a further imperial rebuke, censors audited the monthly delivery tallies and saved more than twenty thousand taels in two months; the audit thereafter became an annual routine.

sentences.zh: 先是上供之物，任土作貢，曰歲辦。

translations.literal: Earlier, goods for imperial tribute were supplied according to local products as tribute, called annual provision.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, imperial tribute followed local products as fixed annual provision.

sentences.zh: 不給，則官出錢以市，曰採辦。

translations.literal: When tribute was insufficient, officials paid money to buy on the market—this was called procurement.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute fell short, officials bought on the market with public funds—this was procurement.

sentences.zh: 其後本折兼收，採辦愈繁。

translations.literal: Later, goods in kind and commutation were collected together, and procurement grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court took both goods in kind and cash commutation, and procurement grew ever more burdensome.

sentences.zh: 於是召商置買，物價多虧，商賈匿跡。

translations.literal: Merchants were then summoned to supply purchases; prices were often short-paid, and traders hid themselves away.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants were conscripted to supply goods at depressed prices, and traders vanished from the markets.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，戶部言：「京師召商納貨取直，富商規避，應役者皆貧弱下戶，請核實編審。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the Ministry of Revenue said: "In the capital, merchants are summoned to deliver goods for payment; wealthy merchants evade service, and those who must serve are poor and weak lower households. We ask for verified registration and review."
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 the Ministry of Revenue reported: "In the capital, conscripted merchants deliver goods for payment, but the rich evade duty and only poor households serve. We ask for a verified household review."

sentences.zh: 」給事中羅崇奎言：「諸商所以重困者，物價賤則減，而貴則不敢增。

translations.literal: " Supervising secretary Luo Chongkui said: "The reason merchants are so heavily afflicted is that when prices fall, payments are cut, but when prices rise they dare not increase them.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising secretary Luo Chongkui said: "Merchants suffer because when prices fall their payment is cut, yet when prices rise they dare not ask for more.

sentences.zh: 且收納不時，一遭風雨，遂不可用，多致賠累。

translations.literal: Moreover, collection is not timely; once goods meet wind and rain they become unusable, and merchants often suffer compensatory losses.
translations.idiomatic: Collection is tardy; one storm ruins the goods, and merchants are left to cover the loss.

sentences.zh: 既收之後，所司更代不常，不即給直，或竟沈閣。

translations.literal: After goods are received, the responsible offices change constantly; payment is not made promptly, or is simply shelved.
translations.idiomatic: After delivery, offices change hands constantly, payment is delayed, and claims are sometimes shelved indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 幸給直矣，官司折閱於上，番役齮齕於下，名雖平估，所得不能半。

translations.literal: Even when payment is given, offices discount it above and runners nibble away below; though called fair valuation, what is received cannot reach half.
translations.idiomatic: Even when paid, offices shave the sum above while runners extort below; though the price is called fair, merchants receive less than half.

sentences.zh: 諸弊若除，商自樂赴，奚用編審。

translations.literal: If these abuses were removed, merchants would gladly come forward—why need registration and review?"
translations.idiomatic: Remove these abuses and merchants will come willingly—there is no need for forced registration."

sentences.zh: 」帝雖納其言，而仍編審如戶部議。

translations.literal: " Although the emperor accepted his words, registration and review still proceeded as the Ministry of Revenue proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice in principle but still carried out the household review the Ministry of Revenue had proposed.

sentences.zh: 穆宗朝，光祿少卿李鍵奏十事，帝乃可之，頗有所減省：停止承天香米、外域珍禽奇獸，罷寶坻魚鮮。

translations.literal: In the Muzong reign, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Li Jian memorialized ten items; the emperor approved, and there were considerable reductions: Chengtian fragrant rice, exotic birds and beasts from foreign lands were stopped, and Baodi fish were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Longqing emperor, Vice Director Li Jian submitted ten reforms; the court approved and cut back sharply: Chengtian fragrant rice, exotic birds and beasts, and Baodi fish were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 凡薦新之物，領於光祿寺，勿遣中官。

translations.literal: All seasonal new offerings were to be received by the Court of Imperial Entertainments; palace eunuchs were not to be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal first-fruits were to be handled by the Court of Imperial Entertainments without dispatching eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 又從太監李芳請，停徵加增細稉米、白青鹽，命一依成、弘間例。

translations.literal: Following eunuch Li Fang's request, levies of added fine glutinous rice and white-green salt were stopped, and all was ordered to follow the Chenghua and Hongzhi precedents.
translations.idiomatic: At eunuch Li Fang's request, added levies of fine glutinous rice and white-green salt were halted, and quotas were restored to the Chenghua and Hongzhi standards.

sentences.zh: 御史王宗載請停加派。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Zongzai requested an end to added levies.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Zongzai asked that supplemental levies be stopped.

sentences.zh: 部議悉準原額，果品百七萬八千餘斤，牲口銀五萬八千餘兩，免加派銀二萬餘。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated to restore all original quotas: fruit at more than 1,078,000 jin, livestock silver at more than fifty-eight thousand taels, and more than twenty thousand taels of added levies were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries agreed to restore original quotas: fruit to 1.078 million jin, livestock silver to fifty-eight thousand taels, and more than twenty thousand taels of supplemental levies were waived.

sentences.zh: 未行，而神宗立，詔免之。

translations.literal: Before this was carried out, Shenzong acceded and by edict remitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the order took effect, the Wanli emperor acceded and remitted the levies by edict.

sentences.zh: 世宗末年，歲用止十七萬兩，穆宗裁二萬，止十五萬餘，經費省約矣。

translations.literal: In the last years of Shizong, annual expenditure was only one hundred seventy thousand taels; Muzong cut twenty thousand, leaving a little more than one hundred fifty thousand—expenses were economized.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Jiajing reign annual spending stood at one hundred seventy thousand taels; the Longqing emperor cut twenty thousand, leaving about one hundred fifty thousand—a real saving.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初年，益減至十三四萬，中年漸增，幾三十萬，而鋪戶之累滋甚。

translations.literal: Early in Wanli it was further reduced to one hundred thirty or forty thousand; in mid-reign it gradually rose to nearly three hundred thousand, while the burden on shop households grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign spending fell to one hundred thirty or forty thousand taels, but by mid-reign it neared three hundred thousand while shopkeepers bore an ever heavier load.

sentences.zh: 時中官進納索賂，名鋪墊錢，費不訾，所支不足相抵，民不堪命，相率避匿。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs who delivered tribute demanded bribes called shop cushion money, at incalculable cost; what was paid out could not offset it, the people could not bear it, and they fled and hid in groups.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs delivering tribute demanded bribes called "shop cushion money" at ruinous cost; official payments could not cover it, and people fled in droves to escape service.

sentences.zh: 乃僉京師富戶為商。

translations.literal: Wealthy households of the capital were then conscripted as merchants.
translations.idiomatic: The court then conscripted wealthy Beijing households as merchant suppliers.

sentences.zh: 令下，被僉者如赴死，重賄營免。

translations.literal: When the order went out, those conscripted were as if going to death, and paid heavy bribes to seek exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When the order went out, the conscripted faced it like a death sentence and paid heavy bribes to escape.

sentences.zh: 官司蜜鉤，若緝奸盜。

translations.literal: Officials set secret traps, as if hunting traitors and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Officials laid secret traps as though hunting criminals.

sentences.zh: 宛平知縣劉曰淑言：「京民一遇僉商，取之不遺毫髮，貲本悉罄。

translations.literal: Wanping magistrate Liu Rishu said: "When capital residents meet merchant conscription, nothing is left—not a hair; their entire capital is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Wanping magistrate Liu Rishu said: "When Beijing residents are conscripted as merchants, they are stripped to the last coin until their capital is gone.

sentences.zh: 請厚估先發，以蘇民困。

translations.literal: Please estimate generously and pay in advance, to relieve the people's distress."
translations.idiomatic: Pay a generous estimate in advance to ease the people's hardship."

sentences.zh: 」御史王孟震斥其越職，曰淑自劾解官去。

translations.literal: " Censor Wang Mengzhen rebuked him for overstepping his office; Rishu memorialized against himself and resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor Wang Mengzhen denounced him for overstepping his authority; Rishu submitted a self-accusation and left office.

sentences.zh: 至熹宗時，商累益重，有輸物於官終不得一錢者。

translations.literal: By the Xizong period the merchants' burden grew still heavier; some delivered goods to officials and in the end received not a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianqi reign the burden had grown worse still: some delivered goods to the government and never received a single coin.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，宮禁中市物，視時估率加十錢，其損上益下如此。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period, when the palace precinct bought goods, it generally added ten cash to the current market estimate—such was its harming the superior to benefit the inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, palace purchases paid ten cash above the market rate—a deliberate policy of favoring sellers over the treasury.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，斥言採五色石者，且以溫州輸礬困民，罷染色布。

translations.literal: Early in Yongle, those who spoke of procuring five-colored stones were rebuked; because Wenzhou's delivery of alum burdened the people, dyed cloth was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign, officials who urged procuring five-colored stones were rebuked; because Wenzhou's alum tribute burdened the people, dyed cloth was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 然內使之出，始於是時。

translations.literal: Yet the dispatch of inner-palace eunuchs began at this time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it was then that palace eunuchs first began to be sent out on procurement.

sentences.zh: 工役繁興，徵取稍急，非土所有，民破產購之。

translations.literal: Labor projects flourished; levies grew somewhat urgent; what was not local to the soil, the people ruined themselves to purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Public works multiplied and levies grew harsher; people ruined themselves buying goods not produced locally.

sentences.zh: 軍器之需尤無算。

translations.literal: Needs for military equipment were especially beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Demand for military equipment was especially boundless.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，山場、園林、湖池、坑冶、果樹、蜂蜜，官設守禁者，悉予民。

translations.literal: In the Renzong period, mountain preserves, gardens, lakes and ponds, mines and smelters, fruit trees, and honey—wherever officials had set guards and prohibitions—were all given to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongxi emperor, mountain preserves, gardens, lakes, mines, orchards, and apiaries under official guard were all returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 宣宗罷閘辦金銀，其他紙靛、糸寧絲、紗羅、ＢＦ緞、香貨、銀鵜硃、金箔、紅花、茜草、麂皮、香蠟、藥物、果品、海味、鵜硃紅戧金龍鳳器物，多所罷減。

translations.literal: The Xuande emperor abolished gate-procured gold and silver; paper, indigo, Ning silk thread, gauze and silk, brocade satin, aromatics, silver cinnabar, gold leaf, safflower, madder, deerskin, fragrant wax, medicines, fruit, seafood, cinnabar-red chased gold dragon-and-phoenix vessels, and the like were largely abolished or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande emperor ended gate-procured gold and silver and sharply cut paper, indigo, Ning silk, gauze, brocade, aromatics, cinnabar, gold leaf, dyes, deerskin, wax, medicines, fruit, seafood, and cinnabar-red chased imperial vessels.

sentences.zh: 副都御史弋謙言：「有司給買辦物料價，十不償一，無異空取。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yi Qian said: "When offices pay prices for procured materials, not one in ten is compensated—it is no different from taking in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yi Qian said: "Offices pay barely one tenth of the price for procured materials—it is outright seizure.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之，諭工部察懲。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted this, and instructed the Ministry of Works to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved and ordered the Ministry of Works to investigate and punish offenders.

sentences.zh: 又因泰安州稅課局大使郝智言，悉召還所遣官，敕自今更不許輒遣，自軍器、軍需外，凡買辦者盡停止。

translations.literal: Also because of the report of Hao Zhi, tax bureau envoy of Tai'an Prefecture, all dispatched officials were recalled; an edict declared that from now on none might be sent at will; apart from military equipment and military supplies, all procurement was to cease.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao Zhi, tax bureau envoy of Tai'an, reported abuses, all dispatched officials were recalled and an edict forbade further arbitrary dispatch; aside from arms and military supplies, all procurement was halted.

sentences.zh: 然寬免之詔屢下，內使屢敕撤還，而奉行不實，宦者輒名採辦，虐取於民。

translations.literal: Yet edicts of leniency and remission were repeatedly issued and eunuchs repeatedly ordered to withdraw, while implementation was not genuine; eunuchs would simply label their actions procurement and cruelly extract from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts of relief were issued again and again and eunuchs were repeatedly ordered to withdraw, yet enforcement was hollow; eunuchs simply called their demands procurement and preyed on the people.

sentences.zh: 誅袁琦、阮巨隊等十餘人，患乃稍息。

translations.literal: More than ten men including Yuan Qi and Ruan Judui were executed, and the trouble then slightly subsided.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten offenders including Yuan Qi and Ruan Judui were executed, and the abuse eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，罷諸處採買及造下西洋船木，諸冗費多敕省。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ying acceded, procurement throughout the realm and timber for building treasure ships for the Western Ocean were abolished; many redundant expenses were ordered cut by edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong emperor acceded, empire-wide procurement and timber for treasure ships were abolished, and many redundant expenses were cut by edict.

sentences.zh: 正統八年，以買辦擾民，始令於存留錢糧內折納，就近解兩京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengtong, because procurement disturbed the people, it was first ordered that commutation be paid from retained grain and money taxes and delivered nearby to the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 8, because procurement harassed the people, the court allowed commutation from retained tax grain and funds to be delivered locally to the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 先是仁宗時，令中官鎮守邊塞，英宗復設各省鎮守，又有守備、分守，中官佈列天下。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Renzong period, palace eunuchs were ordered to garrison the frontier; Emperor Ying restored provincial garrisons, and there were also defense commanders and separate garrisons—eunuchs were spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongxi emperor, eunuchs were posted to garrison the frontiers; the Yingzong emperor restored provincial eunuch garrisons along with defense and sub-garrison posts until eunuchs were stationed across the empire.

sentences.zh: 及憲宗時益甚，購書採藥之使，搜取珍玩，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: By the Chenghua period it grew worse still; envoys to buy books and gather medicines searched out curios, leaving not one survivor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Chenghua emperor the abuse worsened: agents sent to buy books and gather medicines stripped the land of every treasure.

sentences.zh: 抑賣鹽引，私採禽鳥，糜官帑，納私賂，動以巨萬計。

translations.literal: They forced down the sale of salt certificates, privately gathered birds, wasted the public treasury, accepted private bribes—often to the count of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They undersold salt certificates, seized birds privately, squandered public funds, and took bribes running to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 太嶽、太和山降真諸香，通三歲用七千斤，至是倍之。

translations.literal: Aromatics such as jiangzhen from Mount Taiyue and Mount Taihe used seven thousand jin over three years in all; by this time it was doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Incense such as jiangzhen from Mount Taiyue and Mount Taihe had totaled seven thousand jin over three years; now the demand doubled.

sentences.zh: 內府物料，有至五六倍者。

translations.literal: Inner-palace materials in some cases reached five or six times the former amount.
translations.idiomatic: Some inner-palace material quotas rose five- or sixfold.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，頗有減省。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiao acceded, there were considerable reductions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongzhi emperor acceded, the court made substantial cuts.

sentences.zh: 甘肅巡撫羅明言：「鎮守、分守內外官競尚貢獻，各遣使屬邊衛搜方物，名曰採辦，實扣軍士月糧馬價，或巧取番人犬馬奇珍。

translations.literal: Gansu grand coordinator Luo Ming said: "Garrison eunuchs inside and outside the frontier, competing in tribute, each sent agents through border guards to search for local products, calling it procurement but in fact deducting soldiers' monthly grain and horse payments, or craftily seizing fine dogs, horses, and curios from foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu grand coordinator Luo Ming said: "Frontier garrison eunuchs vied in tribute, sending agents through border guards for local products under the name of procurement while docking soldiers' pay and horse funds, or extorting fine horses and curios from foreigners.

sentences.zh: 且設膳乳諸房，僉廚役造酥油諸物。

translations.literal: They also set up kitchens for dairy and the like, conscripting kitchen servants to make butter and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: They also set up dairy kitchens and conscripted cooks to make butter and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 比及起運，沿途騷擾，乞悉罷之。

translations.literal: By the time transport began, disturbances ran along the route—I beg that all this be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: By the time goods were shipped, the route was in turmoil—I ask that all of this be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」報可，然其後靡費漸多。

translations.literal: The reply approved it, but afterward wasteful expenditure gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved, yet thereafter profligate spending steadily mounted.

sentences.zh: 至武宗任劉瑾，漁利無厭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong entrusted Liu Jin, he plundered profit without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wuzong emperor, Liu Jin was given free rein, and his greed for profit knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官率貢銀萬計，皇店諸名不一，歲辦多非土產。

translations.literal: Eunuchs guarding the regions routinely sent tribute silver counted in tens of thousands; imperial shops went by various names; annual supplies were often not local products.
translations.idiomatic: Regional eunuch commanders sent tribute silver by the myriad; imperial shops bore every sort of name, and much of what was levied each year was not even local produce.

sentences.zh: 諸布政使來朝，各陳進貢之害，皆不省。

translations.literal: The regional governors came to court and each explained the harm of tribute presents; none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial governors arrived at court, each laid out the damage done by tribute levies—and none of it was taken to heart.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，內府供應減正德什九。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, inner-palace supplies were reduced to one-tenth of the Zhengde level.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Jiajing reign, supplies to the inner palace were cut to one-tenth of what they had been under Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 中年以後，營建齋醮，採木採香，採珠玉寶石，吏民奔命不暇，用黃白蠟至三十餘萬斤。

translations.literal: After mid-reign, with construction and Taoist rites, gathering timber and incense, gathering pearls, jade, and gemstones, officials and people rushed about with no rest; yellow and white wax used reached more than three hundred thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-reign onward came palace building and Taoist rites, timber to be felled, incense to be gathered, pearls and jade and gems to be sought—officials and commoners ran themselves ragged, and yellow and white wax alone consumed more than three hundred thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 又有召買，有折色，視正數三倍。

translations.literal: There were also compulsory purchases and commutation payments, reaching three times the nominal quota.
translations.idiomatic: There were forced purchases too, and cash commutation in lieu of goods—amounting to three times the stated quota.

sentences.zh: 沈香、降香、海漆諸香至十餘萬斤。

translations.literal: Agarwood, aloeswood, lac resin, and various incense reached more than one hundred thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: Agarwood, aloeswood, lac, and other aromatics ran to more than one hundred thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 又分道購龍涎香，十餘年未獲，使者因請海舶入澳，久乃得之。

translations.literal: They also dispatched separate routes to purchase ambergris; for more than ten years it was not obtained; the envoy therefore requested foreign ships enter Macao, and only after a long time was it obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Ambergris was sought by separate missions; for more than ten years none could be found, until an envoy persuaded foreign vessels to enter Macao—and only then, after long delay, was it secured.

sentences.zh: 方澤、朝日壇，爵用紅黃玉，求不得，購之陝西邊境，遣使覓於阿丹，去土魯番西南二千里。

translations.literal: For the Square Mound and Sun-altar, jade cups used red-yellow jade; unable to obtain it, they purchased it on the Shaanxi frontier and sent envoys to seek it in Aden, two thousand li southwest of Turfan.
translations.idiomatic: For the Square Mound and Sun-altar rites, red-yellow jade was required for the libation cups; when none could be found, buyers were sent to the Shaanxi border, and envoys dispatched to Aden—two thousand li southwest of Turfan.

sentences.zh: 太倉之銀，頗取入承運庫，辦金寶珍珠。

translations.literal: Silver from Taicang was considerably taken into the transport treasury to procure gold, treasures, and pearls.
translations.idiomatic: A large share of Taicang silver was diverted into the transport treasury to fund purchases of gold, jewels, and pearls.

sentences.zh: 於是貓兒睛、祖母碌、石綠、撤孛尼石、紅剌石、北河洗石、金剛鑽、硃藍石、紫英石、甘黃玉，無所不購。

translations.literal: Then cat's-eye, emerald, malachite, zircon, spinel, northern river wash stone, diamond, lapis lazuli, fluorite, and sweet yellow jade—nothing was not purchased.
translations.idiomatic: Cat's-eye, emerald, malachite, zircon, spinel, northern river wash stone, diamond, lapis lazuli, fluorite, sweet yellow jade—there was scarcely a gem the court would not buy.

sentences.zh: 穆宗承之，購珠寶益急。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong inherited this; purchasing pearls and gems became even more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The Longqing emperor inherited the practice, and the hunt for pearls and jewels grew only more frantic.

sentences.zh: 給事中李己、陳吾德疏諫。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Li Ji and Chen Wude memorialized in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Li Ji and Chen Wude submitted memorials of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 己下獄，吾德削籍。

translations.literal: Ji was imprisoned; Wude was stripped of his register.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji was thrown into prison; Chen Wude was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 自是供億浸多矣。

translations.literal: From then on, provisioning gradually increased more and more.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter imperial provisioning swelled year by year.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，內承運庫太監崔敏請買金珠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shenzong's reign, the inner transport treasury eunuch Cui Min requested the purchase of gold and pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, Cui Min, eunuch of the inner transport treasury, petitioned to buy gold and pearls.

sentences.zh: 張居正封還敏疏，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng returned Min's memorial sealed; the matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng sealed and returned Min's memorial, and the matter died there.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝日黷貨，開採之議大興，費以鉅萬計，珠寶價增舊二十倍。

translations.literal: After a long time, the emperor daily indulged in goods; proposals for open extraction flourished; costs counted in vast myriads; gem prices rose twentyfold from before.
translations.idiomatic: In time the emperor's appetite for treasure grew daily; schemes for imperial procurement multiplied; costs ran into vast sums; and the price of jewels climbed to twenty times what it had been.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書陳蕖言庫藏已竭，宜加撙節。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Chen Qu said the treasury was exhausted and thrift should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Chen Qu warned that the coffers were empty and urged strict economy.

sentences.zh: 中旨切責。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from the throne rebuked him in the sharpest terms.

sentences.zh: 而順天府尹以大珠鴉青購買不如旨，鐫級。

translations.literal: The Shuntian prefect, for purchasing large pearls and crow-green jade not meeting the imperial order, was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuntian prefect was reduced in rank for failing to procure large pearls and crow-green jade to the court's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 至於末年，內使雜出，採造益繁。

translations.literal: By the late years, inner envoys went out in various directions; extraction and manufacture became ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the reign, palace eunuchs fanned out on every sort of mission, and procurement and manufacture grew ever more burdensome.

sentences.zh: 內府告匱，至移濟邊銀以供之。

translations.literal: The inner palace reported emptiness, even transferring border relief silver to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace cried destitution, going so far as to divert frontier relief silver to fill its needs.

sentences.zh: 熹宗一聽中官，採造尤夥。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong wholly listened to eunuchs; extraction and manufacture were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianqi emperor deferred entirely to his eunuchs, and procurement and manufacture reached their height.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝立，始務釐剔節省，而庫藏已耗竭矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie succeeded, he began to sort out and save, but the treasury was already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen emperor took the throne, he at last set about reform and retrenchment—but the treasuries were already drained dry.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，後軍都督府供柴炭，役宣府十七衛所軍士採之邊關。

translations.literal: In Yongle, the Rear Military Commission supplied firewood and charcoal, employing soldiers of Xuanfu's seventeen guards to gather it at the border passes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle, the Rear Military Commission supplied firewood and charcoal, conscripting troops from Xuanfu's seventeen guard units to gather it along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，以邊木以扼敵騎，且邊軍不宜他役，詔免其採伐，令歲納銀二萬餘兩，後府召商買納。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, because border timber checked enemy cavalry and border troops should not perform other labor, an edict exempted the gathering and ordered an annual silver payment of more than twenty thousand taels; the rear office summoned merchants to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign, on the grounds that frontier timber blocked enemy cavalry and border troops ought not be diverted to other tasks, an edict ended the logging levy and required instead an annual payment of more than twenty thousand taels of silver, with the rear office contracting merchants to deliver the fuel.

sentences.zh: 四年置易州山廠，命工部侍郎督之，僉北直、山東、山西民夫轉運，而後府輸銀召商如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Yizhou mountain factory was established; a vice-minister of Works was ordered to supervise it; corvée laborers from North Zhili, Shandong, and Shanxi were conscripted for transport; and the rear office paid silver and summoned merchants as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year a mountain depot was set up at Yizhou under a vice-minister of Works; laborers from North Zhili, Shandong, and Shanxi were drafted to haul the timber, while the rear office continued to pay silver and hire merchants as before.

sentences.zh: 初，歲用薪止二千萬餘斤。

translations.literal: Initially, annual firewood use was only more than twenty million jin.
translations.idiomatic: At first annual consumption of firewood ran to little more than twenty million jin.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，增至四千萬餘斤。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi, it increased to more than forty million jin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi it rose to more than forty million jin.

sentences.zh: 轉運既艱，北直、山東、山西乃悉輸銀以召商。

translations.literal: Transport being difficult, North Zhili, Shandong, and Shanxi all paid silver to summon merchants.
translations.idiomatic: As transport grew arduous, North Zhili, Shandong, and Shanxi all switched to paying silver and hiring merchants instead.

sentences.zh: 正德中，用薪益多，增直三萬餘兩。

translations.literal: In Zhengde, firewood use increased further; payments rose by more than thirty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde consumption grew still further, and payments increased by more than thirty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 凡收受柴炭，加耗十之三，中官輒私加數倍。

translations.literal: On all firewood and charcoal received, the surcharge was three-tenths, but eunuchs often privately added several times more.
translations.idiomatic: On every delivery of firewood and charcoal a surcharge of thirty percent was levied—yet eunuchs routinely padded it several times over on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 逋負日積，至以三年正供補一年之耗。

translations.literal: Arrears accumulated day by day, until three years of regular tribute was consumed to cover one year's surcharges.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears piled up daily, until three years of regular quota had to be poured into a single year's surcharges.

sentences.zh: 尚書李鐩議，令正耗相準，而主收者復私加，乃以四萬斤為萬斤，又有輸納浮費，民弗能堪。

translations.literal: Minister Li Fan proposed matching surcharges to regular quotas exactly, but collectors again added privately; they counted forty thousand jin as ten thousand; there were also floating fees on delivery, and the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Fan proposed that surcharges be held to the regular quota—but collectors again padded them in secret, reckoning forty thousand jin as ten thousand, and tacked on extra fees at delivery until the people could endure no more.

sentences.zh: 世宗登極，乃酌減之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he then reviewed and reduced these.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor ascended the throne, he reviewed the levies and cut them back.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，後府採納艱苦，改屬兵部武庫司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing, because gathering and collection by the rear office was arduous, it was transferred to the ordnance bureau of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Longqing, the rear office's procurement having proved too onerous, responsibility passed to the ordnance bureau of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，歲計柴價銀三十萬兩，中官得自徵比諸商，酷刑悉索，而人以惜薪司為陷阱云。

translations.literal: In Wanli, annual charcoal costs totaled three hundred thousand taels of silver; eunuchs collected directly from merchants with cruel torture extracting everything, and people called the firewood office a trap.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, charcoal costs ran to three hundred thousand taels of silver a year; eunuchs collected directly from merchants, torturing them to extract every last coin—and people spoke of the firewood bureau as a snare.

sentences.zh: 廣東珠池，率數十年一採。

translations.literal: Guangdong pearl beds were typically dredged once every several decades.
translations.idiomatic: The pearl beds of Guangdong were dredged, as a rule, only once in several decades.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，有請令中官採東莞珠池者，系之獄。

translations.literal: In Xuande, one who requested that eunuchs dredge the Dongguan pearl beds was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuande reign, a man who proposed sending eunuchs to dredge the Dongguan pearl beds was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 英宗始使中官監守，天順間嘗一採之。

translations.literal: Yingzong first sent eunuchs to guard them; in Tianshun they dredged once.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yingzong eunuchs were first posted as overseers; during Tianshun the beds were dredged once.

sentences.zh: 至弘治十二年，歲久珠老，得最多，費銀萬餘，獲珠二萬八千兩，遂罷監守中官。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year of Hongzhi, the pearls having aged with the years, the yield was greatest; costing more than ten thousand taels of silver, they obtained twenty-eight thousand taels of pearls; then the guarding eunuchs were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: By Hongzhi twelve the pearls, long undisturbed, had matured; the harvest was the richest ever—more than ten thousand taels spent, twenty-eight thousand taels of pearls taken—and the eunuch overseers were then withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 正德九年又採，嘉靖五年又採，珠小而嫩，亦甚少。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde they dredged again; in the fifth year of Jiajing they dredged again; the pearls were small and tender, and very few.
translations.idiomatic: They dredged again in Zhengde nine and Jiajing five, but the pearls were small and immature, and the yield miserably thin.

sentences.zh: 八年復詔採，兩廣巡撫林富言：「五年採珠之役，死者五十餘人，而得珠僅八十兩，天下謂以人易珠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict again ordered dredging. The Guangdong-Guangxi grand coordinator Lin Fu said: "The pearl-gathering labor of the fifth year killed more than fifty people, yet yielded only eighty taels of pearls; the realm said pearls were bought with men's lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year dredging was ordered once more. The grand coordinator of the two Guangs, Lin Fu, wrote: "The pearl levy of the fifth year cost more than fifty lives for a yield of barely eighty taels—the empire called it buying pearls with human flesh."

sentences.zh: 恐今日雖以人易珠，亦不可得。

translations.literal: I fear that even if pearls were bought with men's lives today, they still could not be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that even were we to buy pearls with men's lives today, we should still not obtain them."

sentences.zh: 」給事中王希文言：「雷、廉珠池，祖宗設官監守，不過防民爭奪。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Wang Xiwen said: "The Leizhou and Lianzhou pearl beds—our ancestors posted officials to guard them only to prevent the people from fighting over them.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Wang Xiwen wrote: "At the Leizhou and Lianzhou pearl beds, the founding emperors posted overseers only to keep the people from killing one another in the scramble."

sentences.zh: 正德間，逆豎用事，傳奉採取，流毒海濱。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, wicked minions held power; imperial orders for extraction spread poison along the coast.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, vile favorites held sway; direct imperial orders for extraction poisoned the whole coast.

sentences.zh: 陛下御極，革珠池少監，未久旋復。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty took the throne, you abolished the pearl-bed junior superintendent, but not long after it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, you abolished the junior superintendent of the pearl beds—yet before long the post was restored.

sentences.zh: 驅無辜之民，蹈不測之險，以求不可必得之物，而責以難足之數，非聖政所宜有。

translations.literal: Driving innocent people into unpredictable danger to seek what cannot certainly be obtained, while demanding impossible quotas—this is not what sagely governance should do."
translations.idiomatic: To drive innocent people into mortal peril in pursuit of what may never be found, and to demand quotas impossible to fill—this is not the way of sage rule."

sentences.zh: 」皆不聽。

translations.literal: None of these were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: None of it was heeded.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年詔雲南進寶石二萬塊，廣東採珠八千兩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing, an edict ordered Yunnan to submit twenty thousand gemstone blocks and Guangdong to dredge eight thousand taels of pearls.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing six an edict commanded Yunnan to deliver twenty thousand blocks of precious stone and Guangdong to dredge eight thousand taels of pearls.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，停罷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, these were halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanli took the throne, both orders were suspended.

sentences.zh: 既而乙太后進奉，諸王、皇子、公主冊立、分封、婚禮，令歲辦金珠寶石。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for the Empress Dowager's tribute, and for the investiture, enfeoffment, and wedding rites of princes, imperial sons, and princesses, an order was issued for annual provision of gold, pearls, and gemstones.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, tribute to the Empress Dowager and the investitures, enfeoffments, and weddings of princes, imperial sons, and princesses all required annual levies of gold, pearls, and gems.

sentences.zh: 復遣中官李敬、李鳳廣東採珠五千一百餘兩。

translations.literal: Eunuchs Li Jing and Li Feng were again sent to Guangdong to dredge more than five thousand one hundred taels of pearls.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Li Jing and Li Feng were again dispatched to Guangdong to dredge more than five thousand one hundred taels of pearls.

sentences.zh: 給事中包見捷力諫，不納。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Bao Jianjie remonstrated forcefully; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Bao Jianjie remonstrated with all his force; the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 至三十二年始停採。

translations.literal: Only in the thirty-second year was dredging finally halted.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging was not stopped until the thirty-second year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，以指揮倪英言，復開。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, on the advice of Commander Ni Ying, it was reopened.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year, on the recommendation of Commander Ni Ying, the beds were opened again.

sentences.zh: 明制，兩京織染，內外皆置局。

translations.literal: Under Ming regulation, both capitals had weaving and dyeing; inner and outer bureaus were both established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming institutions, weaving and dyeing were maintained at both capitals, with inner and outer bureaus alike.

sentences.zh: 內局以應上供，外局以備公用。

translations.literal: The inner bureaus supplied the court; the outer bureaus served public needs.
translations.idiomatic: The inner bureaus met imperial demand; the outer bureaus supplied public use.

sentences.zh: 南京有神帛堂、供應機房，蘇、杭等府亦各有織染局，歲造有定數。

translations.literal: Nanjing had the Spirit Silks Hall and supply workshops; Suzhou, Hangzhou, and other prefectures each had weaving and dyeing bureaus, with fixed annual quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing housed the Spirit Silks Hall and supply workshops; Suzhou, Hangzhou, and other prefectures each maintained weaving bureaus with fixed annual output.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，置四川、山西諸行省，浙江紹興織染局。

translations.literal: In Hongwu, weaving and dyeing bureaus were established in Sichuan, Shanxi, and other provinces, and in Shaoxing, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, weaving bureaus were set up in Sichuan, Shanxi, and other provinces, and at Shaoxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 又置藍靛所於儀直、六合，種青藍以供染事。

translations.literal: Indigo farms were also established at Yizhi and Liuhe to grow woad for dyeing.
translations.idiomatic: Indigo farms were also planted at Yizhi and Liuhe to cultivate woad for the dyers.

sentences.zh: 未幾悉罷。

translations.literal: Before long all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they were all abolished.

sentences.zh: 又罷天下有司歲織緞匹。

translations.literal: Annual satin weaving by local officials throughout the realm was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The annual satin levies imposed on local officials throughout the empire were abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 有賞賚，給以絹帛，於後湖置局織造。

translations.literal: When there were rewards, silk was given; a bureau was established at Rear Lake to weave it.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts were paid in silk, woven at a bureau established on Rear Lake.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，復設歙縣織染局。

translations.literal: In Yongle, the Shexian weaving and dyeing bureau was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle the Shexian weaving bureau was re-established.

sentences.zh: 令陝西織造駝毼。

translations.literal: Shaanxi was ordered to weave camel-hair cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was ordered to produce camel-hair felt.

sentences.zh: 正統時，置泉州織造局。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong, a Quanzhou weaving bureau was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong reign a weaving bureau was set up at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天順四年遣中官往蘇、松、杭、嘉、湖五府，於常額外，增造彩緞七千匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun, eunuchs were sent to the five prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou; beyond the regular quota, an additional seven thousand bolts of colored satin were ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun four, eunuchs were dispatched to Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou to weave an extra seven thousand bolts of brocaded satin above the standing quota.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎翁世資請減之，下錦衣獄，謫衡州知府。

translations.literal: Vice-Minister of Works Weng Shizi requested a reduction; he was imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison and demoted to prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Minister of Works Weng Shizi pleaded for a cut—and was thrown into the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison and banished to the prefecture of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 增造坐派於此始。

translations.literal: Mandatory surplus weaving quotas began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the practice of assigning surplus weaving by fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初立，停免蘇、杭、嘉、湖、應天織造。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong first succeeded, weaving in Suzhou, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Yingtian was halted and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi first ascended the throne, weaving at Suzhou, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Yingtian was suspended.

sentences.zh: 其後復設，乃給中官鹽引，鬻於淮以供費。

translations.literal: Afterward it was restored, and eunuchs were given salt vouchers to sell on the Huai River to fund the costs.
translations.idiomatic: When weaving resumed, eunuchs were issued salt certificates to sell along the Huai to cover expenses.

sentences.zh: 萬曆七年，蘇、松水災，給事中顧九思等請取回織造內臣，帝不聽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wanli, Suzhou and Songjiang suffered floods; the supervising secretaries Gu Jiushi and others requested the recall of weaving eunuchs; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli seven, after floods struck Suzhou and Songjiang, Gu Jiushi and other supervising secretaries petitioned to withdraw the weaving eunuchs—the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正力陳年饑民疲，不堪催督，乃許之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng forcefully stated that years of famine had exhausted the people, who could not bear further pressure; permission was then granted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng argued forcefully that years of famine had broken the people and they could bear no more coercion—and at last the court consented.

sentences.zh: 未幾復遣中官。

translations.literal: Before long eunuchs were sent again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the eunuchs were sent back.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，添織漸多。

translations.literal: After Zhang Juzheng died, supplementary weaving gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng's death, extra weaving orders steadily multiplied.

sentences.zh: 蘇、杭、松、嘉、湖五府歲造之外，又令浙江、福建，常、鎮、徽、寧、揚、廣德諸府州分造，增萬餘匹。

translations.literal: Beyond the annual output of the five prefectures of Suzhou, Hangzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, Zhejiang and Fujian and the prefectures and departments of Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Huizhou, Ningguo, Yangzhou, and Guangde were also ordered to share the weaving, adding more than ten thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the standing output of Suzhou, Hangzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, weaving was parcelled out to Zhejiang, Fujian, and the prefectures of Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Huizhou, Ningguo, Yangzhou, and Guangde—adding more than ten thousand bolts to the burden.

sentences.zh: 陝西織造羊絨七萬四千有奇，南直、浙江紵絲、紗羅、綾槹、絹帛，山西潞槹，皆視舊制加丈尺。

translations.literal: Shaanxi wove more than seventy-four thousand units of lambswool; Jiangnan and Zhejiang produced pongee, gauze, satin, and silk; Shanxi Luo satin—all exceeding the old quotas in length and width.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi turned out more than seventy-four thousand lengths of lambswool cloth; Jiangnan and Zhejiang wove pongee, gauze, satin, and plain silk; Shanxi its Luo satin—all cut larger than the old standard by measure.

sentences.zh: 二三年間，費至百萬，取給戶、工二部，蒐括庫藏，扣留軍國之需。

translations.literal: Within two or three years costs reached one million, drawn from the Ministries of Revenue and Works, exhausting storehouses and withholding funds needed for army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Within two or three years expenses ran to a million taels, wrung from the Ministries of Revenue and Works, storehouses scraped bare and military appropriations held back.

sentences.zh: 部臣科臣屢爭，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Ministry officials and censorial officials repeatedly protested; none was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and censors protested again and again—to no avail.

sentences.zh: 末年，復令稅監兼司，奸弊日滋矣。

translations.literal: In the late years, tax supervisors were again assigned dual duties; corruption grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years, tax commissioners were again given charge of weaving as well, and abuse multiplied by the day.

sentences.zh: 明初設南北織染局，南京供應機房，各省直歲造供用，蘇、杭織造，間行間止。

translations.literal: Early Ming established north-south weaving and dyeing bureaus, Nanjing supply workshops, and provincial annual weaving for use; Suzhou and Hangzhou weaving started and stopped intermittently.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's early days, north and south weaving bureaus were set up, Nanjing maintained supply workshops, and the provinces wove on fixed schedules as needed—while Suzhou and Hangzhou operated only from time to time.

sentences.zh: 自萬曆中，頻數派造，歲至十五萬匹，相沿日久，遂以為常。

translations.literal: From mid-Wanli, frequent assigned weaving reached one hundred fifty thousand bolts annually; over time this became customary.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-Wanli onward, repeated imperial orders pushed annual output to one hundred fifty thousand bolts—a figure that, over the years, hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 陝西織造絨袍，弘、正間偶行，嘉、隆時復遣，亦遂沿為常例。

translations.literal: Shaanxi's weaving of wool robes was occasional in Hongzhi and Zhengde; in Jiajing and Longqing it was dispatched again, and this too became a standing practice.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi's wool robes were woven only occasionally under Hongzhi and Zhengde; under Jiajing and Longqing the orders returned—and that too became permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 燒造之事，在外臨清磚廠，京師琉璃、黑窯滄廠，皆造磚瓦，以供營繕。

translations.literal: For kiln firing: outside, the Linqing brick factory; in the capital, the Liuli and Heiyao Cang factories—all made bricks and tiles for construction and repair.
translations.idiomatic: Kiln work was carried on at the Linqing brickworks in the provinces and at the Liuli and Heiyao Cang kilns in the capital—all producing brick and tile for building and repair.

sentences.zh: 宣宗始遣中官張善之饒州，造奉先殿几筵龍鳳文白瓷祭器，磁州造趙府祭器。

translations.literal: Xuande first sent the eunuch Zhang Shan to Raozhou to make white porcelain altar vessels with dragon-phoenix designs for the Ancestral Hall; Cizhou made vessels for Prince Zhao's household.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande the eunuch Zhang Shan was first sent to Raozhou to fire white porcelain altar vessels decorated with dragons and phoenixes for the Ancestral Hall; Cizhou produced ritual ware for the Zhao princely house.

sentences.zh: 逾年，善以罪誅，罷其役。

translations.literal: The next year Shan was executed for crime and the work was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Zhang Shan was executed for his crimes and the commission was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，浮梁民進瓷器五萬餘，償以鈔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, the people of Fuliang presented more than fifty thousand porcelain pieces, compensated with paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong one, the people of Fuliang delivered more than fifty thousand pieces of porcelain, paid for in paper notes.

sentences.zh: 禁私造黃、紫、紅、綠、青、藍、白地青花諸瓷器，違者罪死。

translations.literal: Private manufacture of yellow, purple, red, green, blue, and blue-on-white porcelain was forbidden; violators were punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Private kilns were forbidden to produce yellow, purple, red, green, blue, or blue-on-white wares; offenders faced death.

sentences.zh: 宮殿告成，命造九龍九鳳膳案諸器，既又造青龍白地花缸。

translations.literal: When the palace was completed, an order was issued to make nine-dragon nine-phoenix dining vessels and the like; afterward blue-dragon white-ground flower vats were also ordered.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace was finished, orders went out for dining vessels bearing nine dragons and nine phoenixes, and later for great vats of blue dragon on white ground.

sentences.zh: 王振以為有璺，遣錦衣指揮杖提督官，敕中官往督更造。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen deemed them flawed, sent an Embroidered Uniform Guard commander to beat the supervising official with the rod, and ordered eunuchs to oversee remaking.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen judged them cracked, sent an Embroidered Uniform Guard commander to flog the supervising officer, and dispatched eunuchs to oversee a complete refiring.

sentences.zh: 成化間，遣中官之浮梁景德鎮，燒造御用瓷器，最多且久，費不貲。

translations.literal: In Chenghua, eunuchs were sent to Jingdezhen in Fuliang to fire imperial porcelain; the operation was the largest and longest, and the cost beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chenghua eunuchs were posted to Jingdezhen in Fuliang to fire imperial ware—the largest and longest such operation, at a cost beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初，撤回中官，尋復遣，弘治十五年復撤。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong first succeeded, the eunuchs were withdrawn; soon they were sent again; in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi they were withdrawn once more.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Hongzhi the eunuchs were recalled; soon they were sent back; in Hongzhi fifteen they were recalled again.

sentences.zh: 正德末復遣。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengde they were sent once more.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Zhengde they were dispatched yet again.

sentences.zh: 自弘治以來，燒造未完者三十餘萬器。

translations.literal: Since Hongzhi, more than three hundred thousand unfinished pieces remained from firing.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hongzhi, more than three hundred thousand pieces lay unfinished in the kilns.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，遣中官督之。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing, eunuchs were sent to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing eunuchs were again posted to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳皋謨言其大為民害，請罷之。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Chen Gaomo said it greatly harmed the people and requested its abolition.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Chen Gaomo declared that the operation inflicted grave harm on the people and pleaded for its abolition.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 十六年新作七陵祭器。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, new ritual vessels were made for the seven imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, new ritual vessels were commissioned for the seven imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 三十七年遣官之江西，造內殿醮壇瓷器三萬，後添設饒州通判，專管禦器廠燒造。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year officials were dispatched to Jiangxi to make thirty thousand pieces of porcelain for the inner-hall Daoist altar; afterward an assistant prefect was added at Raozhou to manage exclusively the firing at the Imperial Porcelain Factory.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year officials were sent to Jiangxi to produce thirty thousand pieces of porcelain for the inner-hall Daoist altar; Raozhou later gained an assistant prefect charged solely with overseeing the Imperial Porcelain Factory.

sentences.zh: ，是時營建最繁，近京及蘇州皆有磚廠。

translations.literal: At that time construction works were at their busiest; both near the capital and at Suzhou there were brickworks.
translations.idiomatic: Construction was then at its peak; brickworks operated both near the capital and at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆慶時，詔江西燒造瓷器十餘萬。

translations.literal: During the Longqing reign, an edict ordered Jiangxi to fire more than one hundred thousand pieces of porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longqing, an edict commanded Jiangxi to produce over one hundred thousand pieces of porcelain.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十九年命造十五萬九千，既而復增八萬，至三十八年未畢工。

translations.literal: In Wanli nineteen an order was issued to make one hundred fifty-nine thousand; afterward eighty thousand more were added; by the thirty-eighth year the work was still unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 19 an order called for 159,000 pieces; eighty thousand more were soon added, yet by Wanli 38 the work had still not been completed.

sentences.zh: 自後役亦漸寢。

translations.literal: From then on the labor also gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the labor also tapered off.

sentences.zh: 國家經費，莫大於祿餉。

translations.literal: Of the state's expenditures, none was greater than stipends and salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing strained the state's finances like stipends and salaries.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年定諸王公主歲供之數：親王，米五萬石，鈔二萬五千貫，錦四十匹，紵絲三百匹，紗、羅各百匹，絹五百匹，冬夏布各千匹，綿二千兩，鹽二百引，花千斤，皆歲支。

translations.literal: In Hongwu nine the annual allotments for princes and princesses were fixed: for a full prince, fifty thousand shi of grain, twenty-five thousand guan of notes, forty bolts of brocade, three hundred bolts of ramie silk, one hundred bolts each of gauze and leno, five hundred bolts of silk, one thousand bolts each of summer and winter cloth, two thousand liang of cotton, two hundred yin of salt, and one thousand jin of flowers—all paid yearly.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 9 the court fixed the princes' and princesses' annual allotments: a full prince received fifty thousand shi of grain, twenty-five thousand guan of paper notes, forty bolts of brocade, three hundred bolts of ramie silk, one hundred bolts each of gauze and leno, five hundred bolts of silk, one thousand bolts each of summer and winter cloth, two thousand liang of cotton, two hundred yin of salt, and one thousand jin of flowers, all disbursed yearly.

sentences.zh: 馬料草，月支五十匹。

translations.literal: Horse fodder and hay: fifty bolts monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Horse fodder and hay: fifty bundles per month.

sentences.zh: 其緞匹，歲給匠料，付王府自造。

translations.literal: As for satin bolts, artisans' materials were granted yearly and given to the princely household to manufacture for itself.
translations.idiomatic: Satin was supplied as annual artisan materials for the princely household to weave itself.

sentences.zh: 靖江王，米二萬石，鈔萬貫，餘物半親王，馬料草二十匹。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingjiang received twenty thousand shi of grain and ten thousand guan of notes; other items were half those of a full prince; horse fodder and hay, twenty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingjiang received twenty thousand shi of grain and ten thousand guan of notes, with other items at half a full prince's allotment and twenty bundles of horse fodder and hay.

sentences.zh: 公主未受封者，紵絲、紗、羅各十匹，絹、冬夏布各三十匹，綿二百兩；

translations.literal: Imperial princesses not yet enfeoffed received ten bolts each of ramie silk, gauze, and leno; thirty bolts each of silk and summer and winter cloth; and two hundred liang of cotton;
translations.idiomatic: Princesses not yet enfeoffed received ten bolts each of ramie silk, gauze, and leno, thirty bolts each of silk and summer and winter cloth, and two hundred liang of cotton;

sentences.zh: 已受封，賜莊田一所，歲收糧千五百石，鈔二千貫。

translations.literal: once enfeoffed, they were granted one estate yielding fifteen hundred shi of grain yearly and two thousand guan of notes.
translations.idiomatic: once enfeoffed, they were granted an estate yielding fifteen hundred shi of grain and two thousand guan of notes each year.

sentences.zh: 親王子未受封，視公主；

translations.literal: A prince's sons not yet enfeoffed were treated like princesses;
translations.idiomatic: A prince's unenfeoffed sons were treated like princesses;

sentences.zh: 女未受封者半之。

translations.literal: daughters not yet enfeoffed received half.
translations.idiomatic: unenfeoffed daughters received half that amount.

sentences.zh: 子已受封郡王，米六千石，鈔二千八百貫，錦十匹，紵絲五十匹，紗、羅減紵絲之半，絹、冬夏布各百匹，綿五百兩，鹽五十引，茶三百斤，馬料草十匹。

translations.literal: Sons enfeoffed as commandery princes received six thousand shi of grain, two thousand eight hundred guan of notes, ten bolts of brocade, fifty bolts of ramie silk, gauze and leno at half the ramie silk amount, one hundred bolts each of silk and summer and winter cloth, five hundred liang of cotton, fifty yin of salt, three hundred jin of tea, and ten bolts of horse fodder and hay.
translations.idiomatic: Sons enfeoffed as commandery princes received six thousand shi of grain, two thousand eight hundred guan of notes, ten bolts of brocade, fifty bolts of ramie silk, gauze and leno at half that amount, one hundred bolts each of silk and summer and winter cloth, five hundred liang of cotton, fifty yin of salt, three hundred jin of tea, and ten bundles of horse fodder and hay.

sentences.zh: 女已受封及已嫁，米千石，鈔千四百貫，其緞匹於所在親王國造給。

translations.literal: Daughters already enfeoffed or married received one thousand shi of grain and one thousand four hundred guan of notes; their satin bolts were manufactured and supplied in the full prince's domain where they resided.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed or married daughters received one thousand shi of grain and one thousand four hundred guan of notes; their satin was woven and supplied in the local princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 皇太子之次嫡子並庶子，既封郡王，必俟出閣然後歲賜，與親王子已封郡王者同。

translations.literal: The crown prince's second legitimate son and all sons by concubines, once enfeoffed as commandery princes, had to wait until leaving the palace before receiving annual grants, the same as a prince's sons already enfeoffed as commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's second legitimate son and all sons by concubines, once made commandery princes, received annual grants only after leaving the palace—the same rule as for a prince's sons already enfeoffed as commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 女俟及嫁，與親王女已嫁者同。

translations.literal: Daughters waited until marriage, the same as a prince's daughters already married.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters waited until marriage, on the same terms as a prince's married daughters.

sentences.zh: 凡親王世子，與已封郡王同，郡王嫡長子襲封郡王者，半始封郡王。

translations.literal: Generally a prince's heir-apparent was treated like an enfeoffed commandery prince; the eldest legitimate son of a commandery prince who inherited the title received half the initial allotment of a newly enfeoffed commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: A prince's heir-apparent ranked with an enfeoffed commandery prince; a commandery prince's eldest legitimate son who inherited the title received half the stipend of a newly enfeoffed commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 女已封縣主及已嫁者，米五百石，鈔五百貫，餘物半親王女已受封者。

translations.literal: Daughters enfeoffed as county mistresses or already married received five hundred shi of grain and five hundred guan of notes; other items were half those of a prince's daughter already enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters enfeoffed as county mistresses or already married received five hundred shi of grain and five hundred guan of notes, with other items at half a prince's enfeoffed daughter.

sentences.zh: 郡王諸子年十五，各賜田六十頃，除租稅為永業，其所生子世守之，後乃令止給祿米。

translations.literal: When commandery princes' sons reached fifteen, each was granted sixty qing of land, with rent and tax remitted as perpetual property for their descendants to hold in perpetuity; later the order came to grant only stipend grain.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen, each son of a commandery prince was granted sixty qing of land, rent- and tax-free, for his descendants to hold in perpetuity; later the court restricted the grant to stipend grain alone.

sentences.zh: 二十八年詔以官吏軍士俸給彌廣，量減諸王歲給，以資軍國之用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict declared that because stipends for officials and soldiers had grown ever broader, the princes' annual grants were reduced in measure to fund military and state needs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year an edict held that as official and military pay expanded, princes' annual allotments were scaled back to meet military and state needs.

sentences.zh: 乃更定親王萬石，郡王二千石，鎮國將軍千石，輔國將軍、奉國將軍、鎮國中尉以二百石遞減，輔國中尉、奉國中尉以百石遞減，公主及駙馬二千石，郡王及儀賓八百石，縣主、郡君及儀賓以二百石遞減，縣君、鄉君及儀賓以百石遞減。
