translations.literal: Then it was reset: full princes ten thousand shi, commandery princes two thousand shi, bulwark-state generals one thousand shi, state-assisting generals, state-supporting generals, and bulwark-state commandants decreasing by two hundred shi in succession, state-assisting commandants and state-supporting commandants decreasing by one hundred shi in succession, princesses and imperial sons-in-law two thousand shi, commandery princes and ceremonial consorts eight hundred shi, county mistresses, commandery ladies, and ceremonial consorts decreasing by two hundred shi in succession, township ladies, village ladies, and ceremonial consorts decreasing by one hundred shi in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The court then reset the scale: full princes at ten thousand shi, commandery princes at two thousand shi, bulwark-state generals at one thousand shi, with state-assisting generals, state-supporting generals, and bulwark-state commandants stepping down by two hundred shi each, state-assisting and state-supporting commandants by one hundred shi each, princesses and imperial sons-in-law at two thousand shi, commandery princes and ceremonial consorts at eight hundred shi, county mistresses, commandery ladies, and ceremonial consorts stepping down by two hundred shi each, and township and village ladies and their ceremonial consorts by one hundred shi each.

sentences.zh: 自後為永制。

translations.literal: From then on this became the permanent system.
translations.idiomatic: This thereafter became the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，增減諸王歲祿，非常典也。

translations.literal: When Renzong succeeded, he increased and decreased the princes' annual stipends—this was not regular precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, he adjusted princely stipends up and down—an exceptional measure, not standing practice.

sentences.zh: 時鄭、越、襄、荊、淮、滕、梁七王未之籓，令暫給米歲三千石，遂為例。

translations.literal: At the time the seven princes of Zheng, Yue, Xiang, Jing, Huai, Teng, and Liang had not yet gone to their fiefs; they were ordered temporary grants of three thousand shi of grain yearly, which then became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The seven princes of Zheng, Yue, Xiang, Jing, Huai, Teng, and Liang had not yet departed for their fiefs; they were granted three thousand shi of grain yearly on a temporary basis, and that allowance became precedent.

sentences.zh: 正統十二年定王府祿米，將軍自賜名受封日為始，縣主、儀賓自出閤成婚日為始，於附近州縣秋糧內撥給。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong twelve princely stipend grain was fixed: for generals counting from the day of bestowed title and enfeoffment; for county mistresses and ceremonial consorts from the day of leaving quarters and marriage; allocated from autumn grain of nearby prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 12 princely stipend grain was fixed: for generals from the day title and enfeoffment were granted; for county mistresses and ceremonial consorts from the day they left quarters and married; payment came from autumn grain levies in nearby prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 景泰七年定郡王將軍以下祿米，出閤在前，受封在後，以受封日為始；

translations.literal: In Jingtai seven stipend grain for commandery princes, generals, and below was fixed: if leaving quarters came first and enfeoffment afterward, counting began from the day of enfeoffment;
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 7 stipend grain for commandery princes, generals, and below was fixed: if a prince left quarters before receiving his title, payment began from the day of enfeoffment;

sentences.zh: 受封在前，出閤在後，以出閤日為始。

translations.literal: if enfeoffment came first and leaving quarters afterward, counting began from the day of leaving quarters.
translations.idiomatic: if enfeoffment came first and leaving quarters afterward, payment began from the day he left quarters.

sentences.zh: 宗室有罪革爵者曰庶人。

translations.literal: Members of the imperial clan stripped of rank for crimes were called commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen deprived of rank for crimes were styled commoners.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，頗給以糧。

translations.literal: Early in Yingzong's reign, they were somewhat provided with grain.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingzong's reign they still received a modest grain allowance.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，月支米六石。

translations.literal: Midway through Jiajing, six shi were paid monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing the monthly grant stood at six shi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中減至二石或一石。

translations.literal: Midway through Wanli it was reduced to two shi or one shi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli it fell to two shi or even one.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖大封宗籓，令世世皆食歲祿，不授職任事，親親之誼甚厚。

translations.literal: At first the Founding Emperor enfeoffed the imperial clan on a grand scale, ordering that for generation after generation they should live on annual stipends without appointment to office or public duty—the affection shown kin was very great.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset the Hongwu Emperor enfeoffed the imperial clan on a vast scale, decreeing that for generation after generation they would live on annual stipends without office or public duty—a lavish expression of kinship.

sentences.zh: 然天潢日繁，而民賦有限。

translations.literal: Yet the imperial line daily multiplied, while the people's tax levies were finite.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial line multiplied daily while the people's tax base remained finite.

sentences.zh: 其始祿米盡支本色，既而本鈔兼支。

translations.literal: At first stipend grain was paid entirely in kind; afterward both grain and notes were paid together.
translations.idiomatic: At first stipends were paid wholly in grain; later grain and paper notes were combined.

sentences.zh: 有中半者，有本多於折者，其則不同。

translations.literal: Some received half in kind and half in notes; some received more grain than the conversion rate allowed—the rules differed.
translations.idiomatic: Some received half in kind and half in notes; in some cases grain exceeded the conversion quota—the rules varied.

sentences.zh: 厥後勢不能給，而冒濫轉益多。

translations.literal: Afterward the state could no longer meet the burden, while fraudulent claims grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In time the state could no longer sustain payment, while fraud and abuse only multiplied.

sentences.zh: 奸弊百出，不可究詰。

translations.literal: Corrupt practices sprang up on every side and could not be fully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses proliferated on every side beyond full investigation.

sentences.zh: 自弘治間，禮部尚書倪嶽即條請節減，以寬民力。

translations.literal: From the Hongzhi period onward, Minister of Rites Ni Yue submitted detailed proposals for reduction to ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: From the Hongzhi reign Minister of Rites Ni Yue petitioned for systematic cuts to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十一年，御史林潤言：「天下之事，極弊而大可慮者，莫甚於宗籓祿廩。

translations.literal: In Jiajing forty-one, Censor Lin Run said: "Of all affairs under Heaven, none so utterly corrupt and greatly to be feared as the stipend granaries of the imperial fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 41 Censor Lin Run declared: "Of all affairs under Heaven, nothing is so ruinously corrupt and deeply alarming as the stipend granaries of the imperial fiefs.

sentences.zh: 天下歲供京師糧四百萬石，而諸府祿米凡八百五十三萬石。

translations.literal: The realm's annual grain tribute to the capital is four million shi, yet stipend grain for the various princely establishments totals eight million five hundred thirty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The realm sends four million shi of grain to the capital each year, yet princely establishments consume eight million five hundred thirty thousand shi in stipend grain alone.

sentences.zh: 以山西言，存留百五十二萬石，而宗祿三百十二萬；

translations.literal: Take Shanxi: retained grain one million five hundred twenty thousand shi, yet imperial-clan stipends three million one hundred twenty thousand;
translations.idiomatic: In Shanxi alone, retained grain totals one million five hundred twenty thousand shi, while imperial-clan stipends reach three million one hundred twenty thousand;

sentences.zh: 以河南言，存留八十四萬三千石，而宗祿百九十二萬。

translations.literal: take Henan: retained grain eight hundred forty-three thousand shi, yet imperial-clan stipends one million nine hundred twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: in Henan, retained grain is eight hundred forty-three thousand shi, while imperial-clan stipends reach one million nine hundred twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 是二省之糧，借令全輸，不足供祿米之半，況吏祿、軍餉皆出其中乎？

translations.literal: Even if the grain of these two provinces were wholly delivered, it would not suffice for half the stipend grain—how much less when official salaries and military pay must also come from it?
translations.idiomatic: Even if both provinces delivered every grain they retained, they could not supply half the stipend grain—let alone official salaries and military pay drawn from the same pool.

sentences.zh: 故自郡王以上，猶得厚享，將軍以下，多不能自存，饑寒困辱，勢所必至，常號呼道路，聚詬有司。

translations.literal: Thus from commandery princes upward they still enjoyed generous allotments, while those from generals downward often could not support themselves; hunger, cold, hardship, and humiliation were inevitable, and they constantly cried out in the roads and gathered to revile local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Thus commandery princes and above still lived in comfort, while generals and below often could not support themselves; hunger, cold, and humiliation were inevitable, and they constantly wailed in the streets and gathered to curse local officials.

sentences.zh: 守土之臣，每懼生變。

translations.literal: Local officials always feared that trouble would arise.
translations.idiomatic: Local magistrates lived in constant fear of unrest.

sentences.zh: 夫賦不可增，而宗室日益蕃衍，可不為寒心。

translations.literal: Tax levies cannot be increased, yet the imperial clan daily grows more numerous—can one not shudder at this?
translations.idiomatic: Taxes cannot be raised, yet the imperial clan grows daily—who would not tremble at this?

sentences.zh: 宜令大臣科道集議於朝，且諭諸王以勢窮弊極，不得不通變之意。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order senior ministers and supervising censors to assemble in court for joint deliberation, and also to instruct the princes that circumstances have reached exhaustion and extreme corruption, and that change cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers and supervising censors should be convened for joint deliberation, and the princes should be told plainly that the system has reached exhaustion and that change is unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 令戶部會計賦額，以十年為率，通計兵荒蠲免、存留及王府增封之數。

translations.literal: Let the Ministry of Revenue tally tax quotas, taking ten years as the measure, and calculate together exemptions for war and famine, retained grain, and additions from princely enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Ministry of Revenue tally tax quotas over a ten-year span, accounting together for war and famine exemptions, retained grain, and new princely enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 共陳善後良策，斷自宸衷，以垂萬世不易之規。

translations.literal: Together they should present sound long-term measures for the sovereign's decision, to establish a rule unchanged for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Together they should propose durable remedies for the sovereign's decision, establishing a rule to endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 」下部覆議，從之。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the ministries for review, and the proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went to the ministries for review, and the court approved it.

sentences.zh: 至四十四年乃定宗籓條例。

translations.literal: Only in the forty-fourth year were regulations for the imperial fiefs finally fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Jiajing 44 were regulations for the imperial fiefs finally fixed.

sentences.zh: 郡王、將軍七分折鈔，中尉六分折鈔，郡縣主、郡縣鄉君及儀賓八分折鈔，他冒濫者多所裁減。

translations.literal: Commandery princes and generals received seventy percent in notes; commandants sixty percent in notes; commandery and county ladies, commandery and township ladies, and ceremonial consorts eighty percent in notes; many other fraudulent claims were also cut back.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery princes and generals were paid seventy percent in notes, commandants sixty percent, commandery and county ladies, commandery and township ladies, and ceremonial consorts eighty percent, while many fraudulent claims were also trimmed.

sentences.zh: 於是諸王亦奏辭歲祿，少者五百石，多者至二千石，歲出為稍紓，而將軍以下益不能自存矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the princes also memorialized declining their annual stipends, the lesser by five hundred shi and the greater by as much as two thousand shi; annual outlays were somewhat eased, yet those from generals downward were even less able to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The princes then memorialized to renounce portions of their stipends—some by five hundred shi, others by as much as two thousand—slightly easing annual outlays, yet leaving generals and below even less able to live.

sentences.zh: 明初，勳戚皆賜官田以代常祿。

translations.literal: In early Ming, meritorious officials and imperial kin were all granted official fields in lieu of regular stipends.
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming, meritorious officials and imperial kin received official fields in place of regular stipends.

sentences.zh: 其後令還田給祿米。

translations.literal: Later they were ordered to return the fields and receive stipend grain instead.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were ordered to surrender the fields and take stipend grain instead.

sentences.zh: 公五千石至二千五百石，侯千五百石至千石，伯千石至七百石。

translations.literal: Dukes received from five thousand shi down to two thousand five hundred shi, marquises from one thousand five hundred shi down to one thousand shi, and earls from one thousand shi down to seven hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes received from five thousand to two thousand five hundred shi, marquises from one thousand five hundred to one thousand shi, and earls from one thousand to seven hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 百官之俸，自洪武初，定丞相、御史大夫以下歲祿數，刻石官署，取給於江南官田。

translations.literal: The salaries of all officials: from the beginning of Hongwu, annual stipend amounts were fixed for the chancellor, censor-in-chief, and those below, carved in stone at government offices, and drawn from official fields in the Jiangnan region.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of Hongwu the court fixed annual stipends for the chancellor, censor-in-chief, and all ranks below, carved them on stone at each office, and paid them from official fields in the Jiangnan region.

sentences.zh: ，十三年重定內外文武官歲給祿米、俸鈔之制，而雜流吏典附焉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the system of annual stipend grain and salary notes for civil and military officials inside and outside the capital was reset, with miscellaneous clerks and record keepers included.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the court reset annual stipend grain and salary notes for civil and military officials at court and in the provinces, including miscellaneous clerks and record keepers.

sentences.zh: 正從一二三四品官，自千石至三百石，每階遞減百石，皆給俸鈔三百貫。

translations.literal: Regular and deputy officials of ranks one through four, from one thousand shi down to three hundred shi, decreasing by one hundred shi at each step, all received three hundred guan of salary notes.
translations.idiomatic: Regular and deputy officials of ranks one through four, from one thousand down to three hundred shi in steps of one hundred, each received three hundred guan in salary notes.

sentences.zh: 正五品二百二十石，從減五十石，鈔皆百五十貫。

translations.literal: Regular fifth rank two hundred twenty shi, deputy rank fifty shi less, notes all one hundred fifty guan.
translations.idiomatic: Regular fifth rank received two hundred twenty shi, deputy fifth fifty shi less, with one hundred fifty guan in notes for both.

sentences.zh: 正六品百二十石，從減十石，鈔皆九十貫。

translations.literal: Regular sixth rank one hundred twenty shi, deputy rank ten shi less, notes all ninety guan.
translations.idiomatic: Regular sixth rank received one hundred twenty shi, deputy sixth ten shi less, with ninety guan in notes for both.

sentences.zh: 正從七品視從六品遞減十石，鈔皆六十貫。

translations.literal: Regular and deputy seventh rank followed the deputy sixth rank, decreasing by ten shi at each step, notes all sixty guan.
translations.idiomatic: Regular and deputy seventh rank stepped down from deputy sixth by ten shi each, with sixty guan in notes for both.

sentences.zh: 正八品七十五石，從減五石，鈔皆四十五貫。

translations.literal: Regular eighth rank seventy-five shi, deputy rank five shi less, notes all forty-five guan.
translations.idiomatic: Regular eighth rank received seventy-five shi, deputy eighth five shi less, with forty-five guan in notes for both.

sentences.zh: 正從九品視從八品遞減五石，鈔皆三十貫。

translations.literal: Regular and deputy ninth rank followed the deputy eighth rank, decreasing by five shi at each step, notes all thirty guan.
translations.idiomatic: Regular and deputy ninth rank stepped down from deputy eighth by five shi each, with thirty guan in notes for both.

sentences.zh: 勒之石。

translations.literal: These were carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: The schedule was carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 吏員月俸，一二品官司提控、都吏二石五斗，掾史、令史二石二斗，知印、承差、吏、典一石二斗；

translations.literal: Monthly salaries for clerical staff: at offices of ranks one and two, chief controllers and chief clerks two shi five dou, clerks and record keepers two shi two dou, seal keepers, dispatchers, clerks, and recorders one shi two dou;
translations.idiomatic: Clerical monthly pay: at rank-one and -two offices, chief controllers and chief clerks received two shi five dou, clerks and record keepers two shi two dou, and seal keepers, dispatchers, clerks, and recorders one shi two dou;

sentences.zh: 三四品官司令史、書吏、司吏二石，承差、吏、典半之；

translations.literal: at offices of ranks three and four, office record keepers, scribes, and office clerks two shi, dispatchers, clerks, and recorders half that;
translations.idiomatic: at rank-three and -four offices, office record keepers, scribes, and office clerks two shi, with dispatchers, clerks, and recorders at half that;

sentences.zh: 五品官司司吏一石二斗，吏、典八斗；

translations.literal: at offices of rank five, office clerks one shi two dou, clerks and recorders eight dou;
translations.idiomatic: at rank-five offices, office clerks one shi two dou, clerks and recorders eight dou;

sentences.zh: 六品以下司吏一石；

translations.literal: at rank six and below, office clerks one shi;
translations.idiomatic: at rank six and below, office clerks one shi;

sentences.zh: 光祿寺等吏、典六斗。

translations.literal: clerks and recorders of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the like six dou.
translations.idiomatic: clerks and recorders of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and similar offices six dou.

sentences.zh: 教官之祿，州學正月米二石五斗，縣教諭、府州縣訓導月米二石。

translations.literal: Salaries for educational officers: prefectural schools' chief instructors one shi five dou monthly, county instructors and prefectural, prefectural, and county deputy instructors two shi monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Educational officers' pay: prefectural chief instructors one shi five dou monthly; county instructors and prefectural, departmental, and county deputy instructors two shi monthly.

sentences.zh: 首領官之祿，凡內外官司提控、案牘、州吏目、縣典史皆月米三石。

translations.literal: Salaries for chief officers: all chief controllers, document clerks, departmental sub-officers, and county record keepers at civil and military offices inside and outside the capital received three shi monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Chief officers' pay: chief controllers, document clerks, departmental sub-officers, and county record keepers at civil and military offices inside and outside the capital all received three shi monthly.

sentences.zh: 雜職之祿，凡倉、庫、關、場、司、局、鐵冶、遞運、批驗所大使月三石，副使月二石五斗，河泊所官月米二石，閘壩官月米一石五斗。

translations.literal: Salaries for miscellaneous posts: all granary, treasury, pass, market, bureau, office, ironworks, courier, and inspection station chiefs three shi monthly, deputy chiefs two shi five dou, river-post officers two shi monthly, and sluice and dam officers one shi five dou monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous posts: granary, treasury, pass, market, bureau, office, ironworks, courier, and inspection station chiefs received three shi monthly, deputy chiefs two shi five dou, river-post officers two shi, and sluice and dam officers one shi five dou.

sentences.zh: 天下學校師生廩膳米人日一升，魚肉鹽醯之屬官給之。

translations.literal: Grain for teachers and students at schools throughout the realm was one sheng per person per day; fish, meat, salt, and vinegar and the like were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers and students at schools throughout the realm received one sheng of grain per person per day, with fish, meat, salt, vinegar, and the like supplied by the state.

sentences.zh: 宦官俸，月米一石。

translations.literal: Eunuch salaries: one shi monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs received one shi monthly.

sentences.zh: 二十五年更定百官祿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the salaries of all officials were reset.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the court reset official salaries.

sentences.zh: 正一品月俸米八十七石，從一品至正三品，遞減十三石至三十五石，從三品二十六石，正四品二十四石，從四品二十一石，正五品十六石，從五品十四石，正六品十石，從六品八石，正七品至從九品遞減五斗，至五石而止。

translations.literal: Regular first rank eighty-seven shi monthly; from deputy first rank through regular third rank, decreasing by thirteen shi down to thirty-five shi; deputy third rank twenty-six shi; regular fourth rank twenty-four shi; deputy fourth rank twenty-one shi; regular fifth rank sixteen shi; deputy fifth rank fourteen shi; regular sixth rank ten shi; deputy sixth rank eight shi; from regular seventh rank through deputy ninth rank decreasing by five dou at each step, stopping at five shi.
translations.idiomatic: Regular first rank received eighty-seven shi monthly; deputy first through regular third rank stepped down by thirteen shi to thirty-five shi; deputy third rank twenty-six shi; regular fourth twenty-four shi; deputy fourth twenty-one shi; regular fifth sixteen shi; deputy fifth fourteen shi; regular sixth ten shi; deputy sixth eight shi; ranks seven through nine stepped down by five dou each, stopping at five shi.

sentences.zh: 自後為永制。

translations.literal: From then on this became the permanent system.
translations.idiomatic: This thereafter became the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，官俸全給米，間以錢鈔兼給，錢一千，鈔一貫，抵米一石。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period official salaries were paid entirely in grain, with money and notes occasionally added; one thousand coins or one guan of notes equaled one shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu salaries were paid wholly in grain, with cash and notes occasionally added; one thousand coins or one guan of notes equaled one shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，令公、侯、伯皆全支米；

translations.literal: When Chengzu succeeded, dukes, marquises, and earls all received grain in full;
translations.idiomatic: When Yongle succeeded, dukes, marquises, and earls were paid wholly in grain;

sentences.zh: 文武官俸則米鈔兼支，官高者支米十之四、五，官卑者支米十之六、八；

translations.literal: civil and military salaries were paid in both grain and notes, higher officials receiving four or five tenths in grain and lower officials six or eight tenths in grain;
translations.idiomatic: civil and military officials received grain and notes together, senior ranks four or five tenths in grain and junior ranks six or eight tenths;

sentences.zh: 惟九品、雜職、吏、典、知印、總小旗、軍，並全支米。

translations.literal: only ninth rank, miscellaneous posts, clerks, recorders, seal keepers, chief petty officers, and soldiers all received grain in full.
translations.idiomatic: only ninth rank, miscellaneous posts, clerks, recorders, seal keepers, chief petty officers, and common soldiers were paid wholly in grain.

sentences.zh: 其折鈔者，每米一石給鈔十貫。

translations.literal: For those paid in notes, each shi of grain was exchanged for ten guan of notes.
translations.idiomatic: Where pay was converted to notes, each shi of grain fetched ten guan.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年乃命公、侯、伯視文武官吏，米鈔兼支。

translations.literal: In Yongle two dukes, marquises, and earls were ordered to follow civil and military officials in receiving both grain and notes.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2 dukes, marquises, and earls were placed on the same grain-and-notes schedule as civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，官俸折鈔，每石至二十五貫。

translations.literal: When Renzong succeeded, official salaries converted to notes reached twenty-five guan per shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, the note conversion rate for salaries rose to twenty-five guan per shi.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年，禮部尚書胡濙掌戶部，議每石減十貫，而以十分為準，七分折絹，絹一匹抵鈔二百貫。

translations.literal: In Xuande eight, Minister of Rites Hu Ying, acting head of the Ministry of Revenue, proposed reducing each shi by ten guan and taking ten parts as the standard, with seven parts paid in silk and one bolt of silk equal to two hundred guan of notes.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 8 Minister of Rites Hu Ying, acting as head of the Ministry of Revenue, proposed cutting ten guan per shi and fixing payment at ten parts, seven of silk—with one bolt worth two hundred guan of notes.

sentences.zh: 少師蹇義等以為仁宗在春宮久，深憫官員折俸之薄，故即位特增數倍，此仁政也，詎可違？

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Jian Yi and others held that Renzong, having long served as heir apparent, deeply pitied officials for the thinness of converted salaries, and so upon succeeding had specially increased them several fold—this was benevolent governance; how could it be set aside?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Jian Yi and others argued that Renzong, after long service as heir apparent, had deeply pitied officials for their meager converted pay and upon succeeding had deliberately multiplied it—benevolent governance that must not be undone.

sentences.zh: 濙不聽，竟請於帝而行之，而卑官日用不贍矣。

translations.literal: Hu Ying would not listen and ultimately petitioned the emperor to carry it out, and lower officials could no longer meet daily expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying would not yield and ultimately secured the emperor's approval; junior officials could no longer cover daily expenses.

sentences.zh: 正統中，五品以上米二鈔八，六品以下米三鈔七。

translations.literal: Midway through Zhengtong, fifth rank and above received two parts grain and eight parts notes; sixth rank and below three parts grain and seven parts notes.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Zhengtong, fifth rank and above were paid two parts grain and eight parts notes; sixth rank and below three parts grain and seven parts notes.

sentences.zh: 時鈔價日賤，每石十五貫者已漸增至二十五貫，而戶部尚書王佐復奏減為十五貫。

translations.literal: At the time note values daily fell; what had been fifteen guan per shi gradually rose to twenty-five guan, yet Minister of Revenue Wang Zuo again memorialized reducing it to fifteen guan.
translations.idiomatic: Notes were depreciating daily; what had been fifteen guan per shi had already climbed toward twenty-five, yet Minister of Revenue Wang Zuo memorialized to cut it back to fifteen.

sentences.zh: 成化二年從戶部尚書馬昂請，又省五貫。

translations.literal: In Chenghua two, at the request of Minister of Revenue Ma Ang, another five guan was cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 2, at Minister of Revenue Ma Ang's request, another five guan was lopped off.

sentences.zh: 舊例，兩京文武官折色俸，上半年給鈔，下半年給蘇木、胡椒。

translations.literal: By old precedent, converted salaries for civil and military officials of the two capitals were paid in notes in the first half of the year and in sappanwood and pepper in the second half.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, converted salaries for civil and military officials in the two capitals were paid in notes for the first half of the year and in sappanwood and pepper for the second.

sentences.zh: 七年從戶部尚書楊鼎請，以甲字形檔所積之布估給，布一匹當鈔二百貫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, at the request of Minister of Revenue Yang Ding, cloth stored in the jia-character warehouses was used for payment, one bolt equaling two hundred guan of notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, at Minister of Revenue Yang Ding's request, cloth from the jia-character storehouses was used instead, one bolt worth two hundred guan of notes.

sentences.zh: 是時鈔法不行，一貫僅直錢二三文，米一石折鈔十貫，僅直二三十錢，而布直僅二三百錢，布一匹折米二十石，則米一石僅直十四五錢。

translations.literal: At that time the note system had collapsed; one guan was worth only two or three coins, and one shi of grain converted to ten guan of notes was worth only twenty or thirty coins, while cloth was worth only two or three hundred coins; one bolt converted to twenty shi of grain meant one shi of grain was worth only fourteen or fifteen coins.
translations.idiomatic: By then paper notes had collapsed: one guan fetched only two or three coins, so ten guan for a shi of grain bought barely twenty or thirty coins' worth, while cloth sold for two or three hundred coins; one bolt reckoned at twenty shi meant a shi of grain was worth only fourteen or fifteen coins.

sentences.zh: 自古官俸之薄，未有若此者。

translations.literal: Never in history had official salaries been so thin.
translations.idiomatic: Never in history had official pay been so miserably thin.

sentences.zh: 十六年又令以三梭布折米，每匹抵三十石。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year it was again ordered that three-shuttle cloth be used to convert grain, each bolt equal to thirty shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the court again ordered payment in three-shuttle cloth, each bolt reckoned at thirty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 其後粗闊棉布亦抵三十石，梭布極細者猶直銀二兩，粗布僅直三四錢而已。

translations.literal: Afterward coarse wide cotton cloth also counted for thirty shi; the finest shuttle cloth was still worth two liang of silver, while coarse cloth was worth only three or four coins.
translations.idiomatic: Coarse wide cotton cloth was later valued the same at thirty shi; the finest shuttle cloth still fetched two liang of silver, while coarse cloth was worth only three or four coins.

sentences.zh: 久之，定布一匹折銀三錢。

translations.literal: After a long time, it was fixed that one bolt of cloth was commuted at three mace of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In time the standard was set at three mace of silver per bolt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 於是官員俸給凡二：曰本色，曰折色。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials' salary disbursements were two in all: called payment in kind, called commuted payment.
translations.idiomatic: Official salaries thus came to be paid in two forms: commodities in kind, and commuted payments.

sentences.zh: 其本色有三：曰月米，曰折絹米，曰折銀米。

translations.literal: Its payments in kind had three: called monthly rice, called silk-converted rice, called silver-converted rice.
translations.idiomatic: The in-kind portion had three components: monthly rice, rice commuted from silk, and rice commuted from silver.

sentences.zh: 月米，不問官大小，皆一石。

translations.literal: Monthly rice, regardless of the official's rank high or low, was all one picul.
translations.idiomatic: Every official, whatever his rank, received one picul of monthly rice.

sentences.zh: 折絹，絹一匹當銀六錢。

translations.literal: Silk conversion: one bolt of silk equaled six mace of silver.
translations.idiomatic: For silk commutation, one bolt was reckoned at six mace of silver.

sentences.zh: 折銀，六錢五分當米一石。

translations.literal: Silver conversion: six mace and five candareens equaled one picul of rice.
translations.idiomatic: For silver commutation, six mace five candareens bought one picul of rice.

sentences.zh: 其折色有二：曰本色鈔，曰絹布折鈔。

translations.literal: Its commuted payments had two: called in-kind notes, called silk-and-cloth-converted notes.
translations.idiomatic: The commuted portion had two forms: standard paper notes, and notes derived from silk and cloth conversions.

sentences.zh: 本色鈔十貫折米一石，後增至二十貫。

translations.literal: In-kind notes: ten strings converted to one picul of rice; later it was increased to twenty strings.
translations.idiomatic: Standard notes were first reckoned at ten strings per picul of rice, later raised to twenty.

sentences.zh: 絹布折鈔，絹每匹折米二十石，布一匹折米十石。

translations.literal: Silk-and-cloth-converted notes: each bolt of silk converted to twenty piculs of rice; one bolt of cloth to ten piculs of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Under silk-and-cloth commutation, each bolt of silk counted for twenty piculs of rice, each bolt of cloth for ten.

sentences.zh: 公侯之祿，或本折中半，或折多於本有差。

translations.literal: The stipends of dukes and marquises sometimes were half in kind and half commuted, sometimes the commuted exceeded the in-kind, with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Ducal and marquisate stipends were paid half in kind and half in commuted goods, or with a larger commuted share—arrangements varied.

sentences.zh: 文武官俸，正一品者，本色僅十之三，遞增至從九品，本色乃十之七。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials' salaries: for those of the first grade of the first rank, payment in kind was only three-tenths, increasing in succession to the ninth grade of the second rank, when payment in kind became seven-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Among civil and military salaries, a first-rank, first-grade official received only thirty percent in kind; descending through the ranks to ninth grade, second rank, the in-kind share rose to seventy percent.

sentences.zh: 武職府衛官，惟本色米折銀例，每石二錢五分，與文臣異，餘並同。

translations.literal: Military office officers of guards and battalions differed only in the rule for converting in-kind rice to silver, two mace five candareens per picul, differing from civil officials; the rest was all the same.
translations.idiomatic: For military officers in the guards and battalions, only the silver conversion rate for rice differed—two mace five candareens per picul, not the civil rate; otherwise the terms matched.

sentences.zh: 其三大營副將、參、遊、佐員，每月米五石，巡捕營提督、參將亦如之。

translations.literal: The deputy generals, colonels, brigadiers, and staff officers of the Three Great Camps each received five piculs of rice monthly; the patrol battalion superintendent and colonels were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy generals, colonels, brigadiers, and adjutants of the Three Great Camps drew five piculs of rice a month, as did the patrol battalion superintendent and colonels.

sentences.zh: 巡捕中軍、把總官，月支口糧九斗，旗牌官半之。

translations.literal: Patrol battalion mid-ranking officers and platoon leaders received nine dou of provisions monthly; banner-and-plaque officers received half.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-ranking patrol officers and platoon leaders received nine dou of ration grain monthly; banner officers, half that amount.

sentences.zh: 天下衛所軍士月糧，洪武中，令京外衛馬軍月支米二石，步軍總旗一石五斗，小旗一石二斗，軍一石。

translations.literal: Monthly grain for guard and battalion soldiers throughout the realm: In the Hongwu period, it was ordered that cavalrymen in capital and outer guards received two piculs monthly, infantry company commanders one picul five dou, platoon leaders one picul two dou, common soldiers one picul.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, monthly allotments for garrison troops were fixed: cavalry at two piculs, infantry company commanders at one picul five dou, platoon leaders at one picul two dou, and rank-and-file soldiers at one picul.

sentences.zh: 城守者如數給，屯田者半之。

translations.literal: Those guarding cities received the full amount; those on garrison farms, half.
translations.idiomatic: City garrisons received full rations; troops on colony land, half.

sentences.zh: 民匠充軍者八斗，牧馬千戶所一石，民丁編軍操練者一石，江陰橫海水軍稍班、碇手一石五斗。

translations.literal: Civil artisans serving as soldiers received eight dou; horse-herding sub-battalion offices one picul; militia conscripts drilled as soldiers one picul; Jiangyin and Henghai naval oarsmen and anchor hands one picul five dou.
translations.idiomatic: Artisan conscripts drew eight dou; cavalry ranch offices, one picul; militia trainees, one picul; Jiangyin and Henghai naval oarsmen and anchorsmen, one picul five dou.

sentences.zh: 陣亡病故軍給喪費一石，在營病故者半之。

translations.literal: Soldiers killed in battle or who died of illness were given one picul for funeral expenses; those who died of illness in camp, half.
translations.idiomatic: Families of soldiers killed in action or dead of illness received one picul as a funeral allowance; those who died in camp, half.

sentences.zh: 籍沒免死充軍者謂之恩軍。

translations.literal: Those whose property was confiscated and who were spared death to serve as soldiers were called "favor soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Men spared execution on condition of military service after confiscation of their estates were termed "grace soldiers."

sentences.zh: 家四口以上一石，三口以下六斗，無家口者四斗。

translations.literal: Households of four mouths or more, one picul; three mouths or fewer, six dou; those without household dependents, four dou.
translations.idiomatic: Households of four or more mouths drew one picul; of three or fewer, six dou; men without dependents, four dou.

sentences.zh: 又給軍士月鹽，有家口者二斤，無者一斤，在外衛所軍士以鈔準。

translations.literal: Soldiers were also given monthly salt: those with dependents two jin, those without one jin; outer guard soldiers received the equivalent in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly salt was also issued: two jin for soldiers with families, one for those without; frontier garrisons received the value in paper notes.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，始令糧多之地，旗軍月糧，八分支米，二分支鈔。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period, it was first ordered that in grain-abundant districts, banner soldiers' monthly grain should be eighty percent paid in rice, twenty percent in notes.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle, wealthy regions were first required to pay banner troops eighty percent in grain and twenty percent in notes.

sentences.zh: 後山西、陝西皆然，而福建、兩廣、四川則米七鈔三，江西則米鈔中半，惟京軍及中都留守司，河南、浙江、湖廣軍，仍全支米。

translations.literal: Later Shanxi and Shaanxi were all likewise; but Fujian, the Two Guangs, and Sichuan were seventy percent rice and thirty percent notes, Jiangxi half rice and half notes; only capital troops and those of the Central Capital garrison command, Henan, Zhejiang, and Huguang armies still received wholly in rice.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi and Shaanxi followed suit; Fujian, the Two Guangs, and Sichuan used a seventy-thirty rice-note split, Jiangxi paid half and half; only capital troops, the Zhongdu garrison, and forces in Henan, Zhejiang, and Huguang still drew full rice rations.

sentences.zh: 已而定制，衛軍有家屬者，月米六斗，無者四斗五升，餘皆折鈔。

translations.literal: Thereafter a standard was fixed: guard soldiers with dependents, six dou monthly; without, four dou five sheng; the remainder was all commuted to notes.
translations.idiomatic: A permanent rule followed: six dou for soldiers with families, four dou five sheng for those without, the balance paid in notes.

sentences.zh: 凡各衛調至京操備軍兼工作者，米五斗。

translations.literal: All guard troops transferred to the capital for drilling and assigned additional labor received five dou of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Troops called to the capital for training and spare-duty labor received five dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 其後增損不一，而本折則例，各鎮多寡不同，不能具舉。

translations.literal: Afterward increases and reductions were not uniform; the rules for in-kind and commuted payments differed in amount at each defense command and cannot all be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: Later revisions varied widely; in-kind and commuted rates differed from fortress to fortress and cannot be listed in full.

sentences.zh: 凡各鎮兵餉，有屯糧，有民運，有鹽引，有京運，有主兵年例，有客兵年例。

translations.literal: The military provisions at each defense command included garrison-farm grain, civilian transport, salt certificates, capital transport, annual quotas for resident troops, and annual quotas for guest troops.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier payrolls drew on six sources: colony grain, civilian haulage, salt certificates, grain shipped from the capital, standing-army quotas, and mercenary quotas.

sentences.zh: 屯糧者，明初，各鎮皆有屯田，一軍之田，足贍一軍之用，衛所官吏俸糧皆取給焉。

translations.literal: As for garrison-farm grain: in the early Ming each defense command had garrison farms; one soldier's farmland sufficed for one soldier's consumption, and guard and battalion officers' salary grain was all drawn from it.
translations.idiomatic: Colony grain dated to early Ming, when each frontier post farmed enough land to feed its own troops and to supply officers' salaries.

sentences.zh: 民運者，屯糧不足，加以民糧。

translations.literal: Civilian transport: when garrison-farm grain was insufficient, civilian grain was added.
translations.idiomatic: Where colony harvests fell short, the shortfall was made up by taxes levied on the civilian population.

sentences.zh: 麥、米、豆、草、布、鈔、花絨運給戍卒，故謂之民運，後多議折銀。

translations.literal: Wheat, rice, beans, fodder, cloth, notes, and cotton floss were transported to supply frontier garrisons; hence it was called civilian transport; later it was mostly debated as conversion to silver.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat, rice, beans, fodder, cloth, notes, and cotton were delivered to the border under this "civilian transport" system, though later most dues were commuted to silver.

sentences.zh: 鹽引者，召商入粟開中，商屯出糧，與軍屯相表裏。

translations.literal: Salt certificates: merchants were summoned to deliver grain for certificate issuance; merchant garrison colonies produced grain, mutually supporting military garrison colonies inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Under the salt-certificate system, merchants brought grain to frontier depots to earn trading rights; merchant colonies and military farms worked in tandem.

sentences.zh: 其後納銀運司，名存而實亡。

translations.literal: Later they paid silver to the salt transport office; the name survived but the substance perished.
translations.idiomatic: In time merchants paid silver to salt offices instead—the institution endured in name only.

sentences.zh: 京運，始自正統中。

translations.literal: Capital transport began in the Zhengtong period.
translations.idiomatic: Grain shipped from the capital began during the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 後屯糧、鹽糧多廢，而京運日益矣。

translations.literal: Later garrison-farm grain and salt-financed grain were largely abandoned, and capital transport grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: As colony and salt-tithe grain dwindled, reliance on capital shipments grew ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 主兵有常數，客兵無常數。

translations.literal: Resident troops had fixed numbers; guest troops had no fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Standing garrison strength was fixed; auxiliary and mercenary forces were not.

sentences.zh: 初，各鎮主兵足守其地，後漸不足，增以募兵，募兵不足，增以客兵。

translations.literal: At first each command's resident troops sufficed to defend its territory; later gradually they were insufficient, increased with recruited troops; when recruits were insufficient, increased with guest troops.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, resident troops sufficed to hold each sector; as they thinned out, recruited units were added, and when recruits failed, mercenary "guest" troops.

sentences.zh: 兵愈多，坐食愈眾，而年例亦日增云。

translations.literal: The more troops, the greater the host consuming rations without labor, and the annual quotas also increased daily—thus it is said.
translations.idiomatic: More men meant more idle mouths on the payroll, and annual appropriations climbed steadily.

sentences.zh: 明田稅及經費出入之數，見於掌故進，皆略可考見。

translations.literal: Ming land tax and expenditure and receipt figures appearing in the Record of Precedents can all be investigated in rough outline.
translations.idiomatic: Ming land tax and fiscal receipts and outlays recorded in administrative compilations can still be traced in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年，官民田總八百五十萬七千餘頃。

translations.literal: Hongwu twenty-sixth year: official and private fields totaled more than eight million five hundred seventy thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26, registered official and private fields totaled over 8,507,000 qing.

sentences.zh: 夏稅，米麥四百七十一萬七千餘石，錢鈔三萬九千餘錠，絹二十八萬八千餘匹；

translations.literal: Summer tax: rice and wheat more than four million seven hundred seventeen thousand piculs; cash and notes more than thirty-nine thousand ingots; silk more than two hundred eighty-eight thousand bolts;
translations.idiomatic: Summer levies yielded over 4,717,000 piculs of grain, 39,000-odd ingots of coin and notes, and 288,000 bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 秋糧，米二千四百七十二萬九千餘石，錢鈔五千餘錠。

translations.literal: Autumn grain: rice more than twenty-four million seven hundred twenty-nine thousand piculs; cash and notes more than five thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn grain brought in over 24,729,000 piculs of rice and 5,000-odd ingots of cash and notes.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，官民田總六百二十二萬八千餘頃。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period, official and private fields totaled more than six million two hundred twenty-eight thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, registered fields totaled over 6,228,000 qing.

sentences.zh: 夏稅，米麥四百六十二萬五千餘石，鈔五萬六千三百餘錠，絹二十萬二千餘匹；

translations.literal: Summer tax: rice and wheat more than four million six hundred twenty-five thousand piculs; notes more than fifty-six thousand three hundred ingots; silk more than two hundred two thousand bolts;
translations.idiomatic: Summer revenues were over 4,625,000 piculs of grain, 56,300 ingots of notes, and 202,000 bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 秋糧，米二千二百十六萬六千餘石，鈔二萬一千九百餘錠。

translations.literal: Autumn grain: rice more than twenty-two million one hundred sixty-six thousand piculs; notes more than twenty-one thousand nine hundred ingots.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn grain exceeded 22,166,000 piculs of rice and 21,900 ingots of notes.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，官民田總七百一萬三千餘頃。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, official and private fields totaled more than seven million thirteen thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: During Wanli, registered fields numbered over 7,013,000 qing.

sentences.zh: 夏稅，米麥總四百六十萬五千餘石，起運百九十萬三千餘石，餘悉存留，鈔五萬七千九百餘錠，絹二十萬六千餘匹；

translations.literal: Summer tax: rice and wheat totaled more than four million six hundred five thousand piculs, forwarded more than one million nine hundred three thousand piculs, the remainder all retained locally; notes more than fifty-seven thousand nine hundred ingots; silk more than two hundred six thousand bolts;
translations.idiomatic: Summer grain totaled over 4,605,000 piculs, of which 1,903,000 were forwarded and the rest retained locally; notes exceeded 57,900 ingots; silk, 206,000 bolts;

sentences.zh: 秋糧，米總二千二百三萬三千餘石，起運千三百三十六萬二千餘石，餘悉存留，鈔二萬三千六百餘錠。

translations.literal: Autumn grain: rice totaled more than twenty-two million thirty-three thousand piculs, forwarded more than thirteen million three hundred sixty-two thousand piculs, the remainder all retained locally; notes more than twenty-three thousand six hundred ingots.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn rice totaled over 22,033,000 piculs, with 13,362,000 forwarded and the balance kept in the provinces; notes, 23,600 ingots.

sentences.zh: 屯田六十三萬五千餘頃，花園倉基千九百餘所，徵糧四百五十八萬四千餘石。

translations.literal: Garrison farms more than six hundred thirty-five thousand qing; flower-garden and granary sites more than one thousand nine hundred places; grain levied more than four million five hundred eighty-four thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison land covered over 635,000 qing on 1,900-odd garden and granary plots, yielding 4,584,000 piculs.

sentences.zh: 糧草折銀八萬五千餘兩，布五萬匹，鈔五萬餘貫，各運司提舉大小引鹽二百二十二萬八千餘引。

translations.literal: Grain and fodder commuted to silver more than eighty-five thousand taels; cloth fifty thousand bolts; notes more than fifty thousand strings; salt offices large and small certificate salt more than two million two hundred twenty-eight thousand certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and fodder commuted to over 85,000 taels of silver; cloth dues, 50,000 bolts; paper notes, 50,000 strings; salt offices issued over 2,228,000 certificates of all grades.

sentences.zh: 歲入之數，內承運庫，慈甯、慈慶、乾清三宮子粒銀四萬九千餘兩，金花銀一百一萬二千餘兩，金二千兩。

translations.literal: Figures for annual receipts: Inner Transportation Store, Cining, Ciqing, and Qianqing three palaces' rent silver more than forty-nine thousand taels, "golden flower" silver more than one million twelve thousand taels, gold two thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Annual receipts included over 49,000 taels of estate rents for the Inner Transportation Granary and the Cining, Ciqing, and Qianqing palaces, 1,012,000 taels of "golden-flower" silver, and 2,000 taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 廣惠庫、河西務等七鈔關，鈔二千九百二十八萬餘貫，錢五千九百七十七萬餘文。

translations.literal: Guanghui Store, Hexiwu and six other note barriers, notes more than twenty-nine million two hundred eighty thousand strings, cash more than fifty-nine million seven hundred seventy thousand wen.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanghui treasury and six paper-note customs posts such as Hexiwu contributed over 29,280,000 strings of notes and 59,770,000 wen in cash.

sentences.zh: 京衛屯鈔五萬六千餘貫。

translations.literal: Capital guard garrison notes more than fifty-six thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Capital guard colony notes exceeded 56,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 天財庫、京城九門鈔六十六萬五千餘貫，錢二百四十三萬餘文。

translations.literal: Heavenly Wealth Store, capital nine gates notes more than six hundred sixty-five thousand strings, cash more than two million four hundred thirty thousand wen.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiancai treasury and the nine capital gates yielded over 665,000 strings of notes and 2,430,000 wen in cash.

sentences.zh: 京、通二倉，並薊、密諸鎮漕糧四百萬石。

translations.literal: Capital and Tongzhou two granaries, together with Ji and Miyun and other commands' grain transport, four million piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The capital and Tongzhou granaries, with grain transport from Ji, Miyun, and other commands, totaled four million piculs.

sentences.zh: 京衛屯豆二萬三千餘石。

translations.literal: Capital guard garrison beans more than twenty-three thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Capital guard colony beans exceeded 23,000 piculs.

sentences.zh: 太倉銀庫，南北直隸、浙江、江西、山東、河南派剩麥米折銀二十五萬七千餘兩。

translations.literal: Grand Canal silver store, North Zhili, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Shandong, and Henan surplus wheat and rice commuted to silver more than two hundred fifty-seven thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: The Taicang silver vault held over 257,000 taels from surplus wheat and rice commuted in North Zhili, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 絲綿、稅絲、農桑絹折銀九萬餘兩，綿布、薴布折銀三萬八千餘兩。

translations.literal: Silk floss, tax silk, and mulberry silk commuted to silver more than ninety thousand taels; cotton and ramie cloth commuted to silver more than thirty-eight thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Silk floss, tax silk, and mulberry-silk dues yielded over 90,000 taels; cotton and ramie cloth, over 38,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 百官祿米折銀二萬六千餘兩。

translations.literal: All officials' salary rice commuted to silver more than twenty-six thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Official salary rice commuted to over 26,000 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 馬草折銀三十五萬三千餘兩。

translations.literal: Horse fodder commuted to silver more than three hundred fifty-three thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Horse fodder commutation brought in over 353,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 京五草場折銀六萬三千餘兩。

translations.literal: Capital five fodder grounds commuted to silver more than sixty-three thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's five fodder depots yielded over 63,000 taels in silver commutation.

sentences.zh: 各馬房倉麥豆草折銀二十餘萬兩。

translations.literal: Various horse stables and granaries wheat, beans, and fodder commuted to silver more than two hundred thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat, beans, and fodder from the horse stables and granaries commuted to over 200,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 戶口鹽鈔折銀四萬六千餘兩。

translations.literal: Household salt notes commuted to silver more than forty-six thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Household salt certificates commuted to over 46,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 薊、密、永、昌、易、遼東六鎮，民運改解銀八十五萬三千餘兩。

translations.literal: Ji, Miyun, Yong, Chang, Yi, and Liaodong six commands, civilian transport changed to silver delivery more than eight hundred fifty-three thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian transport dues from the six commands of Ji, Miyun, Yong, Chang, Yi, and Liaodong, converted to silver, totaled over 853,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 各鹽運提舉餘鹽、鹽課、鹽稅銀一百萬三千餘兩。

translations.literal: Various salt transport offices' surplus salt, salt levies, and salt tax silver more than one million three thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus salt, salt levies, and salt taxes from the salt transport offices yielded over 1,003,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 黃白蠟折銀六萬八千餘兩。

translations.literal: Yellow and white wax commuted to silver more than sixty-eight thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow and white wax commutation brought in over 68,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 霸、大等馬房子粒銀二萬三千餘兩。

translations.literal: Ba and Da and other horse stables' rent silver more than twenty-three thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Estate rents from the Ba and Da horse stables and others exceeded 23,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 備邊並新增地畝銀四萬五千餘兩。

translations.literal: Border defense and newly added land acreage silver more than forty-five thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Border-defense and newly registered land taxes yielded over 45,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 京衛屯牧地增銀萬八千餘兩。

translations.literal: Capital guard garrison pasture land additional silver more than eighteen thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Additional revenue from capital guard pasture lands exceeded 18,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 崇文門商稅、牙稅一萬九千餘兩，錢一萬八千餘貫。

translations.literal: Chongwen Gate commercial tax and broker tax more than nineteen thousand taels, cash more than eighteen thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen Gate commercial and broker taxes yielded over 19,000 taels and 18,000 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 張家灣商稅二千餘兩，錢二千八百餘貫。

translations.literal: Zhangjiawan commercial tax more than two thousand taels, cash more than two thousand eight hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangjiawan commercial taxes brought in over 2,000 taels and 2,800 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 諸鈔關折銀二十二萬三千餘兩。

translations.literal: Various note barriers commuted to silver more than two hundred twenty-three thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Paper-note customs posts commuted to over 223,000 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 泰山香稅二萬餘兩。

translations.literal: Mount Tai incense tax more than twenty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tai incense offerings yielded over 20,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 贓罰銀十七萬餘兩。

translations.literal: Fines and confiscations silver more than one hundred seventy thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Fines and confiscated property totaled over 170,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 商稅、魚課、富戶、曆日、民壯、弓兵並屯折、改折月糧銀十四萬四千餘兩。

translations.literal: Commercial tax, fish levies, wealthy-household dues, calendar sales, militia, bow troops, and garrison and revised monthly grain commutation silver more than one hundred forty-four thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Commercial tax, fishing levies, surcharges on wealthy households, calendar sales, militia and archer dues, and colony and revised monthly-ration commutations together exceeded 144,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 北直隸、山東、河南解各邊鎮麥、米、豆、草、鹽鈔折銀八十四萬二千餘兩。

translations.literal: North Zhili, Shandong, and Henan delivered to various border commands wheat, rice, beans, fodder, and salt notes commuted to silver more than eight hundred forty-two thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat, rice, beans, fodder, and salt-note deliveries from North Zhili, Shandong, and Henan to the frontier commands commuted to over 842,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 諸雜物條目繁瑣者不具載。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous items too numerous and trivial to record in full.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous entries too numerous and trivial to list here.

sentences.zh: 所載歲入，但計起運京邊者，而存留不與焉。

translations.literal: The annual receipts recorded count only what was forwarded to the capital and the border, and what was retained locally is not included.
translations.idiomatic: The revenue figures cited count only grain forwarded to the capital and the frontier, not what remained in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 歲出之數，公、侯、駙馬、伯祿米折銀一萬六千餘兩。

translations.literal: Figures for annual expenditures: dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls' salary rice commuted to silver more than sixteen thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Annual outlays included over 16,000 taels for salary rice commuted for dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls.

sentences.zh: 官吏、監生俸米四萬餘石。

translations.literal: Officials' and students' salary rice forty thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Salary rice for officials and imperial students totaled forty thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 官吏折俸絹布銀四萬四千餘兩，錢三千三百餘貫。

translations.literal: Officials' commuted salary silk and cloth silver more than forty-four thousand taels, cash more than three thousand three hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' commuted silk-and-cloth salaries cost over 44,000 taels of silver and 3,300 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 倉庫、草場、官攢、甲鬥，光祿、太常諸司及內府監局匠役本色米八萬六千餘石，折色銀一萬三千餘兩。

translations.literal: Granaries, fodder grounds, official stores, and grain measurers; Guanglu and Taichang various offices and inner palace directorates' artisans and laborers in-kind rice more than eighty-six thousand piculs, commuted silver more than thirteen thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries, fodder depots, government storehouses, and grain measurers; the Guanglu and Taichang bureaus and inner-palace workshops—over 86,000 piculs of in-kind rice and 13,000 taels in commuted pay for artisans and laborers.

sentences.zh: 錦衣等七十八衛所官吏、旗校、軍士、匠役本色米二百一萬八千餘石，折色銀二十萬六千餘兩。

translations.literal: Seventy-eight guards and battalions such as the Embroidered Uniform Guard: officers, bannermen, soldiers, artisans, and laborers in-kind rice more than two million one hundred eighty thousand piculs, commuted silver more than two hundred six thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-eight guards including the Embroidered Uniform Guard—officers, bannermen, soldiers, and artisans—drew over 2,180,000 piculs in kind and 206,000 taels in commuted pay.

sentences.zh: 官員折俸絹布銀二十六萬八千餘兩。

translations.literal: Officials' commuted salary silk and cloth silver more than two hundred sixty-eight thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' commuted silk-and-cloth salaries totaled over 268,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 軍士冬衣折布銀八萬二千餘兩。

translations.literal: Soldiers' winter clothing commuted to cloth silver more than eighty-two thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Winter-clothing cloth commutation for soldiers exceeded 82,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 五軍、神樞、神機三大營將卒本色米十二萬餘石，冬衣折布銀二千餘兩，官軍防秋三月口糧四萬三千餘石，營操馬匹本色料二萬四千餘石，草八十萬餘束。

translations.literal: Five Armies, Divine Pivot, and Divine Engine Three Great Camps officers and soldiers in-kind rice more than one hundred twenty thousand piculs, winter clothing commuted to cloth silver more than two thousand taels, officers and soldiers' three-month autumn-border provisions more than forty-three thousand piculs, camp-drill horses' in-kind fodder more than twenty-four thousand piculs, fodder grass more than eight hundred thousand bundles.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Armies, Divine Pivot, and Divine Engine camps—over 120,000 piculs of ration rice, 2,000 taels for winter-clothing cloth, 43,000 piculs for three months of autumn-border provisions, 24,000 piculs of horse fodder, and 800,000 bundles of hay.

sentences.zh: 巡捕營軍糧七千餘石。

translations.literal: Patrol battalion soldiers' grain more than seven thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol battalion grain rations exceeded 7,000 piculs.

sentences.zh: 京營、巡捕營，錦衣、騰驤諸衛馬料草折銀五萬餘兩。

translations.literal: Capital camps and patrol battalions, Embroidered Uniform and Tengxiang guards and others' horse fodder and grass commuted to silver more than fifty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Horse fodder and hay for the capital camps, patrol battalions, and guards such as the Embroidered Uniform and Tengxiang commuted to over 50,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 中都留守司，山東、河南二都司班軍行糧及工役鹽糧折銀五萬餘兩。

translations.literal: Zhongdu garrison command, Shandong and Henan two regional commands' rotating troops' travel grain and labor salt grain commuted to silver more than fifty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Travel grain and labor-salt grain for rotating troops of the Zhongdu garrison and the Shandong and Henan regional commands commuted to over 50,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 京五草場商價一萬六千餘兩。

translations.literal: Capital five fodder grounds commercial purchase price more than sixteen thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Commercial purchases for the capital's five fodder depots cost over 16,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 御馬三倉象馬等房，商價十四萬八千餘兩。

translations.literal: Imperial horse three granaries, elephant and horse stables and others, commercial purchase price more than one hundred forty-eight thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Commercial purchases for the imperial horse granaries, elephant stables, and related facilities exceeded 148,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 諸邊及近京鎮兵餉。

translations.literal: Various border commands and commands near the capital, military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Military provisions for the frontier commands and those near the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣府：主兵，屯糧十三萬二千餘石，折色銀二萬二千餘兩，民運折色銀七十八萬七千餘兩，兩淮、長蘆、河東鹽引銀十三萬五千餘兩，京運年例銀十二萬五千兩；

translations.literal: Xuanfu: resident troops—garrison grain more than one hundred thirty-two thousand piculs, commuted silver more than twenty-two thousand taels, civilian transport commuted silver more than seven hundred eighty-seven thousand taels, Lianghuai, Changlu, and Hedong salt certificate silver more than one hundred thirty-five thousand taels, capital transport annual quota silver one hundred twenty-five thousand taels;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanfu—resident troops: over 132,000 piculs of colony grain, 22,000 taels in commuted silver, 787,000 taels from civilian transport, 135,000 taels from Lianghuai, Changlu, and Hedong salt certificates, and 125,000 taels in capital-shipment quotas;

sentences.zh: 客兵，淮、蘆鹽引銀二萬六千餘兩，京運年例銀十七萬一千兩。

translations.literal: guest troops—Huai and Lu salt certificate silver more than twenty-six thousand taels, capital transport annual quota silver one hundred seventy-one thousand taels.
